The Deluder of the Three Worlds should be installed with mantras that delude the three worlds,
with a mace on his right, bringing peace, two-armed or four-armed.

63.s:
vāmordhve kārayeccakraṃ pāñcajanyamatho hy adhaḥ /
śrīpuṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ kuryād balena saha bhadrayā //
63.d:
वामोर्ध्वे कारयेच्चक्रं पाञ्चजन्यमथो ह्य् अधः /
श्रीपुष्टिसंयुक्तं कुर्याद् बलेन सह भद्रया //
63.m:
One should have the discus made in his upper left hand, and the Pāñcajanya [conch] below.
One should make him accompanied by Śrī and Puṣṭi, together with Bala and Bhadrā.

63.s:
prāsāde sthāpayedviṣṇuṃ gṛhe vā maṇḍape 'pi vā /
vāmanaṃ caiva vaikuṇṭhaṃ hayāsyamaniruddhakaṃ //
63.d:
प्रासादे स्थापयेद्विष्णुं गृहे वा मण्डपे ऽपि वा /
वामनं चैव वैकुण्ठं हयास्यमनिरुद्धकं //
63.m:
One should install Viṣṇu in a temple, or in a house, or in a pavilion:
Vāmana, Vaikuṇṭha, Hayāsya, and Aniruddha.

63.s:
sthāpayejjalaśayyāsthaṃ matsyādīṃścāvatārakān /
saṅkarṣaṇaṃ viśvarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ vai rudramūrtikaṃ //
63.d:
स्थापयेज्जलशय्यास्थं मत्स्यादींश्चावतारकान् /
सङ्कर्षणं विश्वरूपं लिङ्गं वै रुद्रमूर्तिकं //
63.m:
One should install him resting on the ocean couch, and the incarnations such as the Fish,
Saṅkarṣaṇa, the Universal Form, the liṅga bearing the form of Rudra,

63.s:
ardhanārīśvaraṃ tadvaddhariśaṅkaramātṛkāḥ /
bhairavaṃ ca tathā sūryaṃ grahāṃstadvināyakam //
:n
1 dara dara iti kha, ga, ṅa, iti cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 rakṣa rakṣa oṃ phaṭ iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / rakṣa
rakṣa hrīṃ phaḍiti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 harirūpā sumidvidā iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 185
63.d:
अर्धनारीश्वरं तद्वद्धरिशङ्करमातृकाः /
भैरवं च तथा सूर्यं ग्रहांस्तद्विनायकम् //
:न्
1 दर दर इति ख, ग, ङ, इति चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 रक्ष रक्ष ओं फट् इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / रक्ष
रक्ष ह्रीं फडिति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 हरिरूपा सुमिद्विदा इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 185
63.m:
likewise the Half-Female Lord, Hari-Śaṅkara, the Mothers,
and Bhairava, as well as the Sun, the planets, and Vināyaka;
[...]
1. 'tear, tear' is the reading of the manuscripts marked kha, ga, and ṅa.
2. 'protect, protect, oṃ phaṭ' is the reading of the manuscript marked kha; 'protect, protect, hrīṃ phaṭ' is the reading of the manuscript marked ga.
3. 'possessing the form of Hari, bestowing good knowledge' is the reading of both manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.

63.s:
gaurīmindrādikāṃ lepyāṃ(1) citrajāṃ ca balābalāṃ /
pustakānāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ ca vakṣye likhanatadvidhiṃ //
63.d:
गौरीमिन्द्रादिकां लेप्यां(1) चित्रजां च बलाबलां /
पुस्तकानां प्रतिष्ठां च वक्ष्ये लिखनतद्विधिं //
63.m:
Gaurī, [deities] beginning with Indra, whether made of clay or depicted in paintings, strong or weak;
and I shall explain the consecration of books and the rules for copying them.

63.s:
svastike maṇḍale 'bhyarcya śarapatrāsane sthitaṃ(2) /
lekhyañca likhitaṃ pustaṃ gururvidyāṃ hariṃ yajet //
63.d:
स्वस्तिके मण्डले ऽभ्यर्च्य शरपत्रासने स्थितं(2) /
लेख्यञ्च लिखितं पुस्तं गुरुर्विद्यां हरिं यजेत् //
63.m:
Having worshipped on a svastika maṇḍala [the text] resting on a seat of reed leaves,
the text to be copied and the one already copied, the guru should worship Knowledge and Hari.

63.s:
yajamāno guruṃ vidyāṃ hariṃ lipikṛtaṃ naraṃ /
prāṅmukhaḥ padminīṃ dhyāyet likhitvā ślokapañcakaṃ //
63.d:
यजमानो गुरुं विद्यां हरिं लिपिकृतं नरं /
प्राङ्मुखः पद्मिनीं ध्यायेत् लिखित्वा श्लोकपञ्चकं //
63.m:
The patron, facing east, should meditate upon the lotus-born goddess [Lakṣmī],
having written five verses, worshipping the guru, wisdom, Hari, and the man who serves as the scribe.

63.s:
raupyasthamasyā haimyā ca lekhanyā nāgarākṣaraṃ(3) /
brāhmaṇān bhojayecchakyā śaktyā dadyācca dakṣiṇāṃ(4) //
63.d:
रौप्यस्थमस्या हैम्या च लेखन्या नागराक्षरं(3) /
ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेच्छक्या शक्त्या दद्याच्च दक्षिणां(4) //
63.m:
With ink kept in a silver vessel and a golden pen, in Nāgarī script,
he should feed the brāhmaṇas according to his ability and give sacrificial fee according to his means.

63.s:
guruṃ vidyāṃ hariṃ prārcya purāṇādi likhennaraḥ /
pūrvavanmaṇḍalādye(5) ca aiśānyāṃ bhadrapīṭhake //
63.d:
गुरुं विद्यां हरिं प्रार्च्य पुराणादि लिखेन्नरः /
पूर्ववन्मण्डलाद्ये(5) च ऐशान्यां भद्रपीठके //
63.m:
Having thoroughly worshipped the guru, sacred knowledge, and Hari, a man should write the Purāṇa and the rest,
as before, in the maṇḍala and so forth, on an auspicious seat in the northeast.

63.s:
darpaṇe pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā secayet pūrvavad ghaṭaiḥ /
netronmīlanakaṃ kṛtvā śayyāyāṃ tu nyasennaraḥ //
63.d:
दर्पणे पुस्तकं दृष्ट्वा सेचयेत् पूर्ववद् घटैः /
नेत्रोन्मीलनकं कृत्वा शय्यायां तु न्यसेन्नरः //
63.m:
Having inspected the book in a mirror, he should sprinkle it with jars as before;
having performed the opening of the eyes, a man should place it upon a bed.

63.s:
nyasettu pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ devādyaṃ tatra pustake /
kṛtvā sajīvīkaraṇaṃ prārcya hutvā caruṃ tataḥ //
63.d:
न्यसेत्तु पौरुषं सूक्तं देवाद्यं तत्र पुस्तके /
कृत्वा सजीवीकरणं प्रार्च्य हुत्वा चरुं ततः //
63.m:
He should deposit the Puruṣasūkta and the deities beginning with the supreme deity there upon the book;
having performed the animation, and having worshipped and offered the caru oblation into the fire, then,

63.s:
samprāśya dakṣiṇābhistu gurvādīn bhojayeddvijān /
rathena hastinā vāpi bhrāmyet pustakaṃ naraiḥ(6) //
63.d:
सम्प्राश्य दक्षिणाभिस्तु गुर्वादीन् भोजयेद्द्विजान् /
रथेन हस्तिना वापि भ्राम्येत् पुस्तकं नरैः(6) //
63.m:
having consumed [the remainder], he should feed the Brāhmaṇas beginning with the guru along with sacrificial fees;
and the book should be carried around by men on a chariot or on an elephant.

63.s:
gṛhe devālayādau tu pustakaṃ sthāpya pūjayet /
vastrādiveṣṭitaṃ pāṭhādādāvante samarcayet(7) //
:n
1 indrādikāṃ japyamiti ga, gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 śarayantrāsane sthitamiti kha, gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 raupyamayyātha haimyā vā lekhanyatha varākṣaramiti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 prāṅmukhaḥ padminīṃ dhyāyet likhitvā ca pradāpayet /
brāhmaṇān bhojayecchaktyā śaktyādadyācca dakṣiṇāmiti ga,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 pūrvamaṇḍapapārśve iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 pustakaṃ nara iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
7 ante sadārcayediti kha, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 186
63.d:
गृहे देवालयादौ तु पुस्तकं स्थाप्य पूजयेत् /
वस्त्रादिवेष्टितं पाठादादावन्ते समर्चयेत्(7) //
:न्
1 इन्द्रादिकां जप्यमिति ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 शरयन्त्रासने स्थितमिति ख, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 रौप्यमय्याथ हैम्या वा लेखन्यथ वराक्षरमिति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 प्राङ्मुखः पद्मिनीं ध्यायेत् लिखित्वा च प्रदापयेत् /
ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेच्छक्त्या शक्त्यादद्याच्च दक्षिणामिति ग,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 पूर्वमण्डपपार्श्वे इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 पुस्तकं नर इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
7 अन्ते सदार्चयेदिति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 186
63.m:
Having installed the book in a house, temple, or the like, he should worship it;
wrapped in cloth and other materials, he should worship it at the beginning and the end of the recitation.
[...]
1 "indrādikāṃ japyam" is the reading in the manuscripts marked ga and gha.
2 "śarayantrāsane sthitam" is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha and gha.
3 "raupyamayyātha haimyā vā lekhanyatha varākṣaram" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
4 "prāṅmukhaḥ padminīṃ dhyāyet likhitvā ca pradāpayet
brāhmaṇān bhojayecchaktyā śaktyādadyācca dakṣiṇām" is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
5 "pūrvamaṇḍapapārśve" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
6 "pustakaṃ nara" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
7 "ante sadārcayet" is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha and ga.
[Page 186]

63.s:
jagacchāntiñcāvadhārya pustakaṃ vācayennaraḥ /
adhyāyamekaṃ kumbhādbhiryajamānādi secayet //
63.d:
जगच्छान्तिञ्चावधार्य पुस्तकं वाचयेन्नरः /
अध्यायमेकं कुम्भाद्भिर्यजमानादि सेचयेत् //
63.m:
Having contemplated peace for the world, a man should have the book read;
he should sprinkle the sacrificer and others with water from a jar for one chapter.

63.s:
dvijāya pustakaṃ datvā phalasyānto na vidyate /
trīṇyāhuratidānāni gāvaḥ pṛthvīṃ sarasvatī //
63.d:
द्विजाय पुस्तकं दत्वा फलस्यान्तो न विद्यते /
त्रीण्याहुरतिदानानि गावः पृथ्वीं सरस्वती //
63.m:
Having given a book to a twice-born, there is no end to the fruit;
they speak of three transcendent gifts: cows, the earth, and Sarasvatī.

63.s:
vidyādānaphalaṃ datvā masyantaṃ patrasañcayaṃ /
yāvattu patrasaṅkhyānamakṣarāṇāṃ tathānagha //
63.d:
विद्यादानफलं दत्वा मस्यन्तं पत्रसञ्चयं /
यावत्तु पत्रसङ्ख्यानमक्षराणां तथानघ //
63.m:
Having given the fruit of the gift of learning—the collection of folios down to the ink—
for as many is the count of the folios and likewise of the letters, O sinless one,

63.s:
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṇuloke mahīyate /
pañcarātraṃ purāṇāni bhāratāni dadannaraḥ /
kulaikaviṃśamuddhṛtya pare tattve tu līyate //
:e ity ādimahāputrāṇe āgneye
devādipratiṣṭhāpustakapratiṣṭhākathanaṃ nāma
triṣaṣṭitamodhyāyaḥ
:ś atha catuḥṣaṣṭitamodhyāyaḥ
kūpādipratiṣṭhākathanaṃ
63.d:
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि विष्णुलोके महीयते /
पञ्चरात्रं पुराणानि भारतानि ददन्नरः /
कुलैकविंशमुद्धृत्य परे तत्त्वे तु लीयते //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुत्राणे आग्नेये
देवादिप्रतिष्ठापुस्तकप्रतिष्ठाकथनं नाम
त्रिषष्टितमोध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुःषष्टितमोध्यायः
कूपादिप्रतिष्ठाकथनं
63.m:
for that many thousands of years he is exalted in the world of Viṣṇu.
A man who gives the Pañcarātra, the Purāṇas, and the Mahābhārata,
having rescued twenty-one generations, is dissolved into the supreme reality.
Thus ends the sixty-third chapter, entitled ‘The Account of the Consecration of Deities and Books,’ in the first great Purāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now, the sixty-fourth chapter.
The Account of the Consecration of Wells and Other Waterworks

64.s:
bhagavānuvāca
kūpavāpītaḍāgānāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vacmi tāṃ śṛṇu /
jalarūpeṇa hi hariḥ somo varuṇa uttama //
64.d:
भगवानुवाच
कूपवापीतडागानां प्रतिष्ठां वच्मि तां शृणु /
जलरूपेण हि हरिः सोमो वरुण उत्तम //
64.m:
The Lord said:
I declare the consecration of wells, stepwells, and reservoirs; listen to it.
For Hari is in the form of water, as Soma, and as excellent Varuṇa,

64.s:
agnīṣomamayaṃ viśvaṃ viṣṇurāpastu kāraṇaṃ /
haimaṃ raupyaṃ ratnajaṃ vā varuṇaṃ kārayennaraḥ //
64.d:
अग्नीषोममयं विश्वं विष्णुरापस्तु कारणं /
हैमं रौप्यं रत्नजं वा वरुणं कारयेन्नरः //
64.m:
the universe is made of Agni and Soma, and Viṣṇu is water, the cause.
A man should make [an image of] Varuṇa out of gold, silver, or gemstone,

64.s:
dvibhujaṃ haṃsapṛṣṭhasthaṃ dakṣiṇenābhayapradaṃ /
vāmena nāgapāśaṃ taṃ nadīnāgādisaṃyutaṃ //
64.d:
द्विभुजं हंसपृष्ठस्थं दक्षिणेनाभयप्रदं /
वामेन नागपाशं तं नदीनागादिसंयुतं //
64.m:
two-armed, seated on the back of a swan, granting fearlessness with the right hand,
and with a serpent-noose in his left, accompanied by rivers, nāgas, and others.

64.s:
yāgamaṇḍapamadhye syādvedikā kuṇḍamaṇḍitā /
toraṇaṃ vāruṇaṃ kumbhaṃ nyasecca karakānvitaṃ //
64.d:
यागमण्डपमध्ये स्याद्वेदिका कुण्डमण्डिता /
तोरणं वारुणं कुम्भं न्यसेच्च करकान्वितं //
64.m:
In the middle of the sacrificial pavilion there should be an altar adorned with a fire-pit;
one should erect a gateway, and deposit the jar of Varuṇa along with a pitcher.

64.s:
bhadrake cārdhacandre vā svastike dvāri kumbhakān /
agnyādhānaṃ cāpyakuṇḍe kṛtvā pūrṇāṃ pradāpayet //
:p 187
64.d:
भद्रके चार्धचन्द्रे वा स्वस्तिके द्वारि कुम्भकान् /
अग्न्याधानं चाप्यकुण्डे कृत्वा पूर्णां प्रदापयेत् //
:प् 187

64.s:
varuṇaṃ snānapīṭhe tu ye te śateti saṃspṛśet /
ghṛtenābhyañjayet paścānmūlamantreṇa deśikaḥ //
64.d:
वरुणं स्नानपीठे तु ये ते शतेति संस्पृशेत् /
घृतेनाभ्यञ्जयेत् पश्चान्मूलमन्त्रेण देशिकः //
64.m:
The master should touch Varuṇa upon the bathing pedestal with [the mantra] ‘ye te śataṃ’,
and afterwards anoint him with clarified butter using the basic mantra.

64.s:
śanno devīti prakṣālya śuddhavatyā śivodakaiḥ /
adhivāsayedaṣṭakumbhān sāmudraṃ pūrvakumbhake //
64.d:
शन्नो देवीति प्रक्षाल्य शुद्धवत्या शिवोदकैः /
अधिवासयेदष्टकुम्भान् सामुद्रं पूर्वकुम्भके //
64.m:
Having washed him with ‘śanno devī’ and the Śuddhavatī verses with auspicious water,
he should subject the eight jars to the preliminary consecration: ocean water in the eastern jar,

64.s:
gāṅgamagnau varṣatoyaṃ dakṣe rakṣastu nairjharaṃ /
nadītoyaṃ paścime tu vāyavye tu nadodakaṃ //
64.d:
गाङ्गमग्नौ वर्षतोयं दक्षे रक्षस्तु नैर्झरं /
नदीतोयं पश्चिमे तु वायव्ये तु नदोदकं //
64.m:
Gaṅgā water in the southeast, rainwater in the south, waterfall water in the southwest,
river water in the west, and stream water in the northwest;

64.s:
audbhijjaṃ cottare sthāpya aiśānyāṃ tīrthasambhavaṃ /
alābhe tu nadītoyaṃ(1) yāsāṃ rājeti mantrayet(2) //
64.d:
औद्भिज्जं चोत्तरे स्थाप्य ऐशान्यां तीर्थसम्भवं /
अलाभे तु नदीतोयं(1) यासां राजेति मन्त्रयेत्(2) //
64.m:
and having placed spring water in the north, and water from a sacred ford in the northeast;
if unobtainable, he should consecrate river water with the mantra ‘yāsāṃ rājā’.

64.s:
devaṃ nirmārjya nirmañchya durmitriyeti vicakṣaṇaḥ(3) /
netre conmīlayeccitraṃ taccakṣurmadhuratrayaiḥ //
64.d:
देवं निर्मार्ज्य निर्मञ्छ्य दुर्मित्रियेति विचक्षणः(3) /
नेत्रे चोन्मीलयेच्चित्रं तच्चक्षुर्मधुरत्रयैः //
64.m:
The wise priest, having wiped and cleansed the deity with [the mantra] ‘durmitriyā’,
should open his wonderful eyes with the three sweets with [the verse] ‘taccakṣuḥ’.

64.s:
jyotiḥ sampūrayeddhaimyāṃ gurave gāmathārpayet /
samudrajyeṣṭhetyabhiṣiñcayedvaruṇaṃ pūrvakumbhataḥ //
64.d:
ज्योतिः सम्पूरयेद्धैम्यां गुरवे गामथार्पयेत् /
समुद्रज्येष्ठेत्यभिषिञ्चयेद्वरुणं पूर्वकुम्भतः //
64.m:
He should fill [the eyes with] light using a golden [needle], and then give a cow to the guru.
He should consecrate Varuṇa with [the mantra] ‘samudrajyeṣṭhāḥ’ from the eastern jar;

64.s:
samudraṃ gaccha gāṅgeyāt somo dhenviti varṣakāt /
devīrāpo nirjharādbhir nadādbhiḥ pañcanadyataḥ //
64.d:
समुद्रं गच्छ गाङ्गेयात् सोमो धेन्विति वर्षकात् /
देवीरापो निर्झराद्भिर् नदाद्भिः पञ्चनद्यतः //
64.m:
with ‘samudraṃ gaccha’ from the Gaṅgā water; with ‘somo dhenuḥ’ from the rainwater;
with ‘devīrāpaḥ’ from the waterfall water; with [the waters of] the five rivers from the stream water;

64.s:
udbhidadbhyaścodbhidena pāvamānyātha tīrthakaiḥ /
āpo hi ṣṭhā pañcagavyāddhiraṇyavarṇeti svarṇajāt //
64.d:
उद्भिदद्भ्यश्चोद्भिदेन पावमान्याथ तीर्थकैः /
आपो हि ष्ठा पञ्चगव्याद्धिरण्यवर्णेति स्वर्णजात् //
64.m:
with the spring water from spring [mantras]; then with the Pāvamānī hymns from the waters of sacred fords;
with ‘āpo hi ṣṭhā’ from the five products of the cow; with ‘hiraṇyavarṇāḥ’ from golden water;

64.s:
āpo asmeti varṣoptyair vyāhṛtyā kūpasambhavaiḥ /
varuṇañca taḍāgoptyair varuṇādbhistu vaśyataḥ //
64.d:
आपो अस्मेति वर्षोप्त्यैर् व्याहृत्या कूपसम्भवैः /
वरुणञ्च तडागोप्त्यैर् वरुणाद्भिस्तु वश्यतः //
64.m:
with ‘āpo asmān’ from waters sown by rain; with the sacred utterances from well water;
and Varuṇa with waters sown in reservoirs; and with waters of Varuṇa for subduing;

64.s:
āpo devīti girijair ekāśīvighaṭaistataḥ /
snāpayedvaruṇasyeti tvanno varuṇā cārghyakaṃ //
64.d:
आपो देवीति गिरिजैर् एकाशीविघटैस्ततः /
स्नापयेद्वरुणस्येति त्वन्नो वरुणा चार्घ्यकं //
64.m:
with ‘āpo devīḥ’ with mountain water, then with eighty-one jars
he should bathe him with ‘varuṇasya’ and offer the water offering with ‘tvanno varuṇa’;

64.s:
vyāhṛtyā madhuparkantu vṛhaspateti vastrakaṃ /
varuṇeti pavitrantu praṇavenottarīyakaṃ //
:n
1 nadīkṣodamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 āsāṃ rudreti kīrtayediti ṅa, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 indriyeti vicakṣaṇa iti ga, gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 188
64.d:
व्याहृत्या मधुपर्कन्तु वृहस्पतेति वस्त्रकं /
वरुणेति पवित्रन्तु प्रणवेनोत्तरीयकं //
:न्
1 नदीक्षोदमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 आसां रुद्रेति कीर्तयेदिति ङ, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 इन्द्रियेति विचक्षण इति ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 188
64.m:
the honey-mixture with the sacred utterances; the garment with ‘bṛhaspate’;
the sacred thread with ‘varuṇa’; and the upper garment with the Praṇava;
[...]
1 "nadīkṣodam" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2 "āsāṃ rudreti kīrtayet" is the reading in the manuscripts marked ṅa and ga.
3 "indriyeti vicakṣaṇaḥ" is the reading in the manuscripts marked ga and gha.
[Page 188]

64.s:
yadvāraṇyena puṣpādi pradadyādvaruṇāya tu /
cāmaraṃ darpaṇaṃ chatraṃ vyajanaṃ vaijayantikāṃ //
64.d:
यद्वारण्येन पुष्पादि प्रदद्याद्वरुणाय तु /
चामरं दर्पणं छत्रं व्यजनं वैजयन्तिकां //
64.m:
with ‘yadvāraṇyena’ he should offer flowers and the rest to Varuṇa,
a fly-whisk, a mirror, a parasol, a fan, and a banner.

64.s:
mūlenottiṣṭhetyutthāpya tāṃ rātrimadhivāsayet /
varuṇañceti sānnidhyaṃ yadvāraṇyena pūjayet //
64.d:
मूलेनोत्तिष्ठेत्युत्थाप्य तां रात्रिमधिवासयेत् /
वरुणञ्चेति सान्निध्यं यद्वारण्येन पूजयेत् //
64.m:
Having raised him up with the basic mantra and ‘uttiṣṭha’, he should keep him for the preliminary consecration that night;
and invoking presence with ‘varuṇañca’, he should worship with ‘yadvāraṇyena’.

64.s:
sajīvīkaraṇaṃ mūlāt punargandhādinā yajet /
maṇḍape(1) pūrvavat prārcya kuṇḍeṣu samidādikaṃ //
64.d:
सजीवीकरणं मूलात् पुनर्गन्धादिना यजेत् /
मण्डपे(1) पूर्ववत् प्रार्च्य कुण्डेषु समिदादिकं //
64.m:
Having performed animation from the basic mantra, he should worship again with perfumes and the like.
Having worshipped in the pavilion as before, and [having placed] firewood and other materials into the fire-pits,

64.s:
vedādimantrair gandhādyāś catasro dhenavo duhet /
dikṣvatho vai yavacaruṃ tataḥ saṃsthāpya homayet(2) //
64.d:
वेदादिमन्त्रैर् गन्धाद्याश् चतस्रो धेनवो दुहेत् /
दिक्ष्वथो वै यवचरुं ततः संस्थाप्य होमयेत्(2) //
64.m:
he should milk four cows endowed with perfumes and other offerings with the mantras beginning with the Vedas;
and then, placing barley caru in the directions, he should make fire oblations;

64.s:
vyāhṛtyā vātha gāyatryā mūlenāmantrayettathā /
sūryāya prajāpataye dyauḥ svāhā cāntarikṣakaḥ //
64.d:
व्याहृत्या वाथ गायत्र्या मूलेनामन्त्रयेत्तथा /
सूर्याय प्रजापतये द्यौः स्वाहा चान्तरिक्षकः //
64.m:
or with the sacred utterances, or with the Gāyatrī, he should likewise invoke with the basic mantra:
‘To Sūrya, to Prajāpati, svāhā to Heaven, and to the Antarikṣa,’

64.s:
tasyai pṛthivyai dehadhṛtyai iha svadhṛtaye tataḥ /
iha ratyai ceha ramatyā ugro bhīmaś ca raudrakaḥ //
64.d:
तस्यै पृथिव्यै देहधृत्यै इह स्वधृतये ततः /
इह रत्यै चेह रमत्या उग्रो भीमश् च रौद्रकः //
64.m:
‘to that Earth, for bodily preservation, here for self-preservation,’ then
‘here for delight, and here for rejoicing; Ugra, Bhīma, and Raudra,’

64.s:
viṣṇuś ca varuṇo dhātā rāyaspoṣo mahendrakaḥ(3) /
agniryamo nairṛto 'tha varuṇo vāyureva ca //
64.d:
विष्णुश् च वरुणो धाता रायस्पोषो महेन्द्रकः(3) /
अग्निर्यमो नैरृतो ऽथ वरुणो वायुरेव च //
64.m:
‘and Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, Rāyaspoṣa, Mahendra,
Agni, Yama, Nairṛta, and Varuṇa and Vāyu,’

64.s:
kuvera īśo 'nanto 'tha brahmā rājā jaleśvaraḥ /
tasmai svāhedaṃ viṣṇuś ca tadviprāseti homayet //
64.d:
कुवेर ईशो ऽनन्तो ऽथ ब्रह्मा राजा जलेश्वरः /
तस्मै स्वाहेदं विष्णुश् च तद्विप्रासेति होमयेत् //
64.m:
‘Kuvera, Īśa, Ananta, then Brahmā the king, the lord of waters;
svāhā to him,’ and he should make fire oblations with ‘idaṃ viṣṇuḥ’ and ‘tadviprāsaḥ’;

64.s:
somo dhenviti ṣaḍ hutvā imaṃ meti ca homayet /
āpo hi ṣṭheti tisṛbhirimā rudreti homayet //
64.d:
सोमो धेन्विति षड् हुत्वा इमं मेति च होमयेत् /
आपो हि ष्ठेति तिसृभिरिमा रुद्रेति होमयेत् //
64.m:
having offered six oblations with ‘somo dhenuḥ’, he should also offer with ‘imaṃ me’;
he should offer with the three verses ‘āpo hi ṣṭhā’ and with ‘imā rudra’.

64.s:
daśādikṣu baliṃ dadyāt gandhapuṣpādinārcayet /
pratimāṃ tu samutthāpya maṇḍale vinyased budhaḥ //
64.d:
दशादिक्षु बलिं दद्यात् गन्धपुष्पादिनार्चयेत् /
प्रतिमां तु समुत्थाप्य मण्डले विन्यसेद् बुधः //
64.m:
He should present bali offerings in the ten directions and worship with perfumes, flowers, and the like;
and the wise man, having raised up the image, should place it in the maṇḍala.

64.s:
pūjayedgandhapuṣpādyair hemapuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt /
:n
1 maṇḍale iti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 mūle tvagnau ca homayediti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 vāyuḥ somo mahendraka iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 189
jalāśayāṃstu digbhāge vitastidvayasammitān //
64.d:
पूजयेद्गन्धपुष्पाद्यैर् हेमपुष्पादिभिः क्रमात् /
:न्
1 मण्डले इति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 मूले त्वग्नौ च होमयेदिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 वायुः सोमो महेन्द्रक इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 189
जलाशयांस्तु दिग्भागे वितस्तिद्वयसम्मितान् //
64.m:
He should worship it with perfumes, flowers, and the like, and with golden flowers and so on in due order,
[...]
1 "maṇḍale" is the reading in both manuscripts marked kha and ṅa.
2 "mūle tvagnau ca homayet" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
3 "vāyuḥ somo mahendrakaḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
[Page 189]
and the water basins in the directional regions measuring two spans.

64.s:
kṛtvāṣṭau sthaṇḍilān ramyān saikatān deśikottamaḥ /
varuṇasyeti mantreṇa sājyamaṣṭaśataṃ tataḥ //
64.d:
कृत्वाष्टौ स्थण्डिलान् रम्यान् सैकतान् देशिकोत्तमः /
वरुणस्येति मन्त्रेण साज्यमष्टशतं ततः //
64.m:
Having prepared eight pleasant sandy mounds, the excellent spiritual master
[should offer] one hundred and eight [oblations] with clarified butter using the mantra beginning with "Of Varuṇa".

64.s:
caruṃ yavamayaṃ hutvā(1) śāntitoyaṃ samācaret /
secayenmūrdhni devaṃ tu sajīvakaraṇaṃ caret //
64.d:
चरुं यवमयं हुत्वा(1) शान्तितोयं समाचरेत् /
सेचयेन्मूर्ध्नि देवं तु सजीवकरणं चरेत् //
64.m:
Having offered sacrificial boiled barley, he should perform the pacification water rite;
he should sprinkle [water] on the head of the god and perform the enlivening rite.

64.s:
dhyāyettu varuṇaṃ yuktaṃ gauryā nadanadīgaṇaiḥ /
oṃ varuṇāya namo 'bhyarcya tataḥ sānnidhyamācaret //
64.d:
ध्यायेत्तु वरुणं युक्तं गौर्या नदनदीगणैः /
ओं वरुणाय नमो ऽभ्यर्च्य ततः सान्निध्यमाचरेत् //
64.m:
He should meditate on Varuṇa united with Gaurī and the hosts of rivers and streams;
having worshipped with "Om, obeisance to Varuṇa," he should then effect his presence.

64.s:
utthāpya(2) nāgapṛṣṭhādyair bhrāmayettaiḥ samaṅgalaiḥ /
āpo hi ṣṭheti ca kṣipettrimadhvākte ghaṭe jale //
64.d:
उत्थाप्य(2) नागपृष्ठाद्यैर् भ्रामयेत्तैः समङ्गलैः /
आपो हि ष्ठेति च क्षिपेत्त्रिमध्वाक्ते घटे जले //
64.m:
Having raised [him], he should carry [the vessel] around on the back of an elephant and the like with auspicious rites;
and with "The waters indeed are," he should place [him] in water, in a jar smeared with the three sweets.

64.s:
jalāśaye madhyagataṃ suguptaṃ viniveśayet /
snātvā dhyāyecca varuṇaṃ sṛṣṭiṃ brahmāṇḍasañjñikāṃ //
64.d:
जलाशये मध्यगतं सुगुप्तं विनिवेशयेत् /
स्नात्वा ध्यायेच्च वरुणं सृष्टिं ब्रह्माण्डसञ्ज्ञिकां //
64.m:
He should deposit [it] well concealed, reaching the center of the water reservoir;
having bathed, he should meditate upon Varuṇa and creation named the cosmic egg.

64.s:
agnivījena sandagddhya tadbhasma plāvayeddharāṃ /
sarvamapomayaṃ lokaṃ dhyāyet tatra jaleśvaraṃ //
64.d:
अग्निवीजेन सन्दग्द्ध्य तद्भस्म प्लावयेद्धरां /
सर्वमपोमयं लोकं ध्यायेत् तत्र जलेश्वरं //
64.m:
Having burned [the cosmos] with the fire-seed-syllable, he should inundate the earth with its ashes;
he should meditate upon the entire world as consisting of water, and therein upon the Lord of the Waters.

64.s:
toyamadhyasthitaṃ devaṃ tato yūpaṃ niveśayet /
caturasramathāṣṭāsraṃ vartulaṃ vā pravartitaṃ(3) //
64.d:
तोयमध्यस्थितं देवं ततो यूपं निवेशयेत् /
चतुरस्रमथाष्टास्रं वर्तुलं वा प्रवर्तितं(3) //
64.m:
Then, [regarding] the god standing in the midst of the water, he should install a sacrificial post,
four-cornered, octagonal, or made round.

64.s:
ārādhya devatāliṅgaṃ daśahastaṃ tu kūpake /
yūpaṃ yajñīyavṛkṣotthaṃ mūle haimaṃ phalaṃ nyaset //
64.d:
आराध्य देवतालिङ्गं दशहस्तं तु कूपके /
यूपं यज्ञीयवृक्षोत्थं मूले हैमं फलं न्यसेत् //
64.m:
Having worshipped the mark of the deity, [the post should be] ten cubits [long] in a well,
a sacrificial post made from a sacrificial tree; at its root he should place a golden fruit.

64.s:
vāpyāṃ pañcadaśakaraṃ puṣkariṇyāṃ tu viṃśatikaṃ /
taḍāge pañcaviṃśākhyaṃ jalamadhye niveśayet //
64.d:
वाप्यां पञ्चदशकरं पुष्करिण्यां तु विंशतिकं /
तडागे पञ्चविंशाख्यं जलमध्ये निवेशयेत् //
64.m:
Fifteen cubits in a step-well, twenty in a lotus pond,
called twenty-five [cubits] in a reservoir, he should install it in the middle of the water.

64.s:
yāgamaṇḍapāṅgeṇa vā yūpabrasketi mantrataḥ (4) /
sthāpya tadveṣṭayedvastrair yūpopari patākikāṃ //
:n
1 caruṃ sacamasaṃ hutveti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 utthāya iti kha, ga, gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 suvartitamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 yūpasthāneti mantrata iti ga, gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 190
64.d:
यागमण्डपाङ्गेण वा यूपब्रस्केति मन्त्रतः (4) /
स्थाप्य तद्वेष्टयेद्वस्त्रैर् यूपोपरि पताकिकां //
:न्
1 चरुं सचमसं हुत्वेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 उत्थाय इति ख, ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 सुवर्तितमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 यूपस्थानेति मन्त्रत इति ग, घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 190
64.m:
Or, with a limb of the sacrificial pavilion, with the mantra "O sacrificial post cutter,"
having set it up, he should wrap it with garments and place a small flag atop the sacrificial post.
[...]
1. "Having offered sacrificial boiled food with a sacrificial spoon" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "Having arisen" is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha, ga, and gha.
3. "Well-rounded" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
4. "With the mantra 'at the place of the sacrificial post'" is the reading in the manuscripts marked ga, gha, and ṅa.

64.s:
tadabhyarcya ca gandhādyair jagacchāntiṃ samācaret /
dakṣiṇāṃ gurave dadyādbhūgohemāmbupātrakaṃ //
64.d:
तदभ्यर्च्य च गन्धाद्यैर् जगच्छान्तिं समाचरेत् /
दक्षिणां गुरवे दद्याद्भूगोहेमाम्बुपात्रकं //
64.m:
Having worshipped that with perfumes and the like, he should perform universal pacification;
he should give a sacrificial fee to the guru: land, a cow, gold, and a water-pot.

64.s:
dvijebhyo dakṣiṇā deyā āgatān bhojayettathā /
ābrahmastambaparyantā ye kecitsalilārthinaḥ //
64.d:
द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणा देया आगतान् भोजयेत्तथा /
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्ता ये केचित्सलिलार्थिनः //
64.m:
A sacrificial fee should be given to the twice-born, and he should likewise feed those who have arrived:
"Whosoever from Brahmā down to a clump of grass are desirous of water,

64.s:
te tṛptimupagacchantu taḍāgasthena vāriṇā /
toyamutsarjayedevaṃ(1) pañcagavyaṃ vinikṣipet //
64.d:
ते तृप्तिमुपगच्छन्तु तडागस्थेन वारिणा /
तोयमुत्सर्जयेदेवं(1) पञ्चगव्यं विनिक्षिपेत् //
64.m:
may they attain satisfaction from the water in this reservoir."
In this manner he should release the water, and he should pour in the five bovine products.

64.s:
āpo hi ṣṭheti tisṛbhiḥ śāntitoyaṃ dvijaiḥ kṛtaṃ /
tīrthatoyaṃ kṣipet puṇyaṃ gokulañcārpayedvijān(2) //
64.d:
आपो हि ष्ठेति तिसृभिः शान्तितोयं द्विजैः कृतं /
तीर्थतोयं क्षिपेत् पुण्यं गोकुलञ्चार्पयेद्विजान्(2) //
64.m:
The pacification water prepared by the twice-born with the three verses beginning "The waters indeed are,"
and auspicious sacred ford water he should pour, and he should present a herd of cows to the twice-born.

64.s:
anivāritamannādyaṃ sarvajanyañca kārayet /
aśvamedhasahasrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ yaḥ samācaret //
64.d:
अनिवारितमन्नाद्यं सर्वजन्यञ्च कारयेत् /
अश्वमेधसहस्राणां सहस्रं यः समाचरेत् //
64.m:
He should provide unhindered food and the like for all people;
he who might perform a thousand thousand horse sacrifices,

64.s:
ekāhaṃ sthāpayettoyaṃ tatpuṇyamayutāyutaṃ /
/.vimāne modate svarge narakaṃ na sa gacchati //
64.d:
एकाहं स्थापयेत्तोयं तत्पुण्यमयुतायुतं /
/.विमाने मोदते स्वर्गे नरकं न स गच्छति //
64.m:
if he maintains water for a single day, that merit is myriadfold;
he rejoices in heaven in a celestial chariot and does not go to hell.

64.s:
gavādi pivate yasmāttasmāt kartur na pātakaṃ /
toyadānātsarvadānaphalaṃ prāpya divaṃ yajet //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye
kūpavāpītaḍāgādipratiṣṭhākathanaṃ nāma
catuḥṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sabhāsthāpanakathanaṃ
64.d:
गवादि पिवते यस्मात्तस्मात् कर्तुर् न पातकं /
तोयदानात्सर्वदानफलं प्राप्य दिवं यजेत् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये
कूपवापीतडागादिप्रतिष्ठाकथनं नाम
चतुःषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
सभास्थापनकथनं
64.m:
Since cows and other [beings] drink from it, there is no sin for the builder;
from the gift of water, having obtained the fruit of all gifts, he worships heaven.
Thus in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa of Agni, the sixty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Consecration of Wells, Step-Wells, Reservoirs, and Other [Water Works]".
Now, the sixty-fifth chapter.
The Description of the Establishment of an Assembly Hall.

65.s:
bhagavānuvāca
sabhādisthānaṃ vakṣye tathaiva teṣāṃ pravartanaṃ /
bhūmau parīkṣitāyāñca vāstuyāgaṃ samācaret //
65.d:
भगवानुवाच
सभादिस्थानं वक्ष्ये तथैव तेषां प्रवर्तनं /
भूमौ परीक्षितायाञ्च वास्तुयागं समाचरेत् //

65.s:
svecchayā tu sabhāṃ kṛtvā svecchayā sthāpayet surān /
:n
1 toyaṃ samutsṛjedevamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gokulaṃ pāyayed dvijāniti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 191
catuṣpathe grāmādau(1) ca na śūnye kārayet sabhāṃ //
65.d:
स्वेच्छया तु सभां कृत्वा स्वेच्छया स्थापयेत् सुरान् /
:न्
1 तोयं समुत्सृजेदेवमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गोकुलं पाययेद् द्विजानिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 191
चतुष्पथे ग्रामादौ(1) च न शून्ये कारयेत् सभां //
65.m:
Having built an assembly hall according to his wish, he should install the gods according to his wish.
[...]
1. "In this manner he should release the water" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "He should make the twice-born drink the herd of cows" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
He should construct the assembly hall at a crossroads, in a village or the like, but not in a desolate place.

65.s:
nirmalaḥ kulamuddhṛtya kartā svarge vimodate /
anena vidhinā kuryāt saptabhaumaṃ harergṛhaṃ //
65.d:
निर्मलः कुलमुद्धृत्य कर्ता स्वर्गे विमोदते /
अनेन विधिना कुर्यात् सप्तभौमं हरेर्गृहं //
65.m:
The builder, purified and delivering his family, rejoices in heaven;
by this rule he should make a seven-storied house for Hari.

65.s:
yathā rājñāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ pūrvādyāś ca dhvajādayaḥ /
koṇabhujān varjayitvā catuḥśālaṃ tu vartayet //
65.d:
यथा राज्ञां तथान्येषां पूर्वाद्याश् च ध्वजादयः /
कोणभुजान् वर्जयित्वा चतुःशालं तु वर्तयेत् //
65.m:
As for kings, so for others, the flag and other [characteristics] are in the east and the other directions;
avoiding corner limbs, he should lay out a four-winged building,

65.s:
triśālaṃ vā dviśālaṃ vā ekaśālamathāpi vā /
vyayādhikaṃ na kurvīta vyayadoṣakaraṃ hi tat //
65.d:
त्रिशालं वा द्विशालं वा एकशालमथापि वा /
व्ययाधिकं न कुर्वीत व्ययदोषकरं हि तत् //
65.m:
or a three-winged, or a two-winged, or even a single-winged [building];
he should not make the expenditure greater [than the income], for that causes the defect of loss.

65.s:
āyādhike bhavet pīḍā tasmāt kuryāt samaṃ dvayaṃ /
kararāśiṃ samastantu kuryādvasuguṇaṃ guruḥ //
65.d:
आयाधिके भवेत् पीडा तस्मात् कुर्यात् समं द्वयं /
करराशिं समस्तन्तु कुर्याद्वसुगुणं गुरुः //
65.m:
If income is excessive, there will be affliction; therefore he should make the two equal;
the guru should multiply the entire sum of cubits by eight.

65.s:
saptārciṣā hṛte bhāge gargavidyāvicakṣaṇaḥ /
aṣṭadhā bhājite tasmin yaccheṣaṃ sa vyayo gataḥ //
65.d:
सप्तार्चिषा हृते भागे गर्गविद्याविचक्षणः /
अष्टधा भाजिते तस्मिन् यच्छेषं स व्ययो गतः //
65.m:
When divided by seven, one learned in the science of Garga [calculates]:
when that is divided eightfold, whatever is the remainder, that constitutes the expenditure.

65.s:
athavā kararāśiṃ tu hanyāt saptārciṣā budhaḥ /
vasubhiḥ saṃhṛte bhāge pṛthvyādi(2) parikalpayet //
65.d:
अथवा करराशिं तु हन्यात् सप्तार्चिषा बुधः /
वसुभिः संहृते भागे पृथ्व्यादि(2) परिकल्पयेत् //
65.m:
Or the wise man should multiply the sum of cubits by seven;
when that part is divided by eight, he should determine the earth and other elements,

65.s:
dhvajo dhūmras tathā siṃhaḥ śvā vṛṣastu kharo gajaḥ /
tathā dhvāṅkṣastu pūrvādāvudbhavanti vikalpayet //
65.d:
ध्वजो धूम्रस् तथा सिंहः श्वा वृषस्तु खरो गजः /
तथा ध्वाङ्क्षस्तु पूर्वादावुद्भवन्ति विकल्पयेत् //
65.m:
the flag, smoke, lion, dog, bull, donkey, elephant,
and crow—these arise in the east and other [directions], and he should calculate them.

65.s:
triśālakatrayaṃ śastaṃ udakpūrvavivarjitaṃ /
yāmyāṃ paragṛhopetaṃ dviśālaṃ labhyate sadā //
65.d:
त्रिशालकत्रयं शस्तं उदक्पूर्वविवर्जितं /
याम्यां परगृहोपेतं द्विशालं लभ्यते सदा //
65.m:
A group of three wings is praiseworthy when devoid of the north and east wings;
a two-winged [house] containing houses in the south and west is always recommended.

65.s:
yāmye śālaikaśālaṃ tu pratyakśālamathāpi vā /
ekaśāladvayaṃ śastaṃ śeṣāstvanye bhayāvahāḥ //
65.d:
याम्ये शालैकशालं तु प्रत्यक्शालमथापि वा /
एकशालद्वयं शस्तं शेषास्त्वन्ये भयावहाः //
65.m:
A single-winged [house] with a wing in the south, or with a wing in the west—
these two single-winged types are commendable, while the others are dangerous.

65.s:
catuḥśālaṃ sadā śastaṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitaṃ /
ekabhaumādi kurvīta bhavanaṃ saptabhaumakaṃ //
65.d:
चतुःशालं सदा शस्तं सर्वदोषविवर्जितं /
एकभौमादि कुर्वीत भवनं सप्तभौमकं //
65.m:
A four-winged [house] is always commendable, free from all defects;
he should build a residence from one story up to seven stories,

65.s:
dvāravedyādirahitaṃ pūraṇena vivarjitaṃ /
devagṛhaṃ devatāyāḥ pratiṣṭhāvidhinā sadā //
:n
1 pūś catuṣpathagrāmādāviti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 dhvajādi iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 192
65.d:
द्वारवेद्यादिरहितं पूरणेन विवर्जितं /
देवगृहं देवतायाः प्रतिष्ठाविधिना सदा //
:न्
1 पूश् चतुष्पथग्रामादाविति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 ध्वजादि इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 192
65.m:
free from door-altars and the like, and free from fill-in material;
a house of God should always [be made] for the deity by the rule of consecration.
[...]
1. "In the east, at a crossroads, in a village or the like" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "The flag and others" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.

65.s:
saṃsthāpya manujānāñca samudāyoktakarmaṇā /
prātaḥ sarvauṣadhīsnānaṃ kṛtvā śuciratandritaḥ //
65.d:
संस्थाप्य मनुजानाञ्च समुदायोक्तकर्मणा /
प्रातः सर्वौषधीस्नानं कृत्वा शुचिरतन्द्रितः //
65.m:
Having installed it by the rite prescribed for the collective of human beings,
having taken a bath with all herbs in the morning, pure and untiring,

65.s:
madhuraistu dvijān bhojya pūrṇakumbhādiśobhitaṃ /
satoraṇaṃ svasti vācya dvijān goṣṭhahastakaḥ(1) //
65.d:
मधुरैस्तु द्विजान् भोज्य पूर्णकुम्भादिशोभितं /
सतोरणं स्वस्ति वाच्य द्विजान् गोष्ठहस्तकः(1) //
65.m:
having fed the twice-born with sweet things, [the house] adorned with full jars and the like,
endowed with an archway, having caused the twice-born to recite auspicious blessings, holding [cow dung from] the cow-pen in his hand,

65.s:
gṛhī gṛhaṃ praviśecca daivajñān prārcya(2) saṃviśet /
gṛhe puṣṭikaraṃ mantraṃ paṭheccemaṃ samāhitaḥ //
65.d:
गृही गृहं प्रविशेच्च दैवज्ञान् प्रार्च्य(2) संविशेत् /
गृहे पुष्टिकरं मन्त्रं पठेच्चेमं समाहितः //
65.m:
the householder should enter the house; having first worshipped the astrologers, he should enter;
and he should recite this prosperity-bestowing mantra in the house with a concentrated mind:

65.s:
oṃ nande nandaya vāśiṣṭhe vasubhiḥ prajayā saha /
jaye bhārgavadāyade prajānāṃ vijayāvahe //
65.d:
ओं नन्दे नन्दय वाशिष्ठे वसुभिः प्रजया सह /
जये भार्गवदायदे प्रजानां विजयावहे //
65.m:
"Om, O Nandā, cause rejoicing, O daughter of Vasiṣṭha, along with the Vasus and with progeny!
O Jayā, O inheritor of Bhṛgu, bringer of victory to offspring!

65.s:
pūrṇe 'ṅgirasadāyāde pūrṇakāmaṃ kurudhva māṃ /
bhadre kāśyapadāyāde kuru bhadrāṃ matiṃ mama //
65.d:
पूर्णे ऽङ्गिरसदायादे पूर्णकामं कुरुध्व मां /
भद्रे काश्यपदायादे कुरु भद्रां मतिं मम //
65.m:
O Pūrṇā, inheritor of Aṅgiras, make my desires fulfilled!
O Bhadrā, inheritor of Kaśyapa, make my mind auspicious!

65.s:
sarvavījauṣadhīyukte sarvaratnauṣadhīvṛte /
rucire nandane nande vāsiṣṭhe ramyatāmiha //
65.d:
सर्ववीजौषधीयुक्ते सर्वरत्नौषधीवृते /
रुचिरे नन्दने नन्दे वासिष्ठे रम्यतामिह //
65.m:
Endowed with all seeds and herbs, surrounded by all gems and herbs,
charming, delightful, O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, take delight here!

65.s:
prajāpatisute devi caturasre mahīyasi /
subhage suvrate devi gṛhe kāśyapi ramyatāṃ //
65.d:
प्रजापतिसुते देवि चतुरस्रे महीयसि /
सुभगे सुव्रते देवि गृहे काश्यपि रम्यतां //
65.m:
O daughter of Prajāpati, O goddess, four-cornered, most exalted,
fortunate, observing good vows, O goddess, daughter of Kaśyapa, take delight in this house!

65.s:
pūjite paramācāryair gandhamālyair alaṅkṛte /
bhavabhūtikare devi gṛhe bhārgavi ramyatāṃ //
65.d:
पूजिते परमाचार्यैर् गन्धमाल्यैर् अलङ्कृते /
भवभूतिकरे देवि गृहे भार्गवि रम्यतां //
65.m:
Worshipped by supreme teachers, adorned with perfumes and garlands,
causing worldly prosperity, O goddess, daughter of Bhṛgu, take delight in this house!"

65.s:
avyakte vyākṛte pūrṇe muneraṅgirasaḥ sute /
iṣṭake tvaṃ prayaccheṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayāmyahaṃ //
65.d:
अव्यक्ते व्याकृते पूर्णे मुनेरङ्गिरसः सुते /
इष्टके त्वं प्रयच्छेष्टं प्रतिष्ठां कारयाम्यहं //
65.m:
O unmanifest one, manifest one, full one, daughter of the sage Aṅgiras!
O brick, grant what is desired; I perform the consecration.

65.s:
deśasvāmipurasvāmigṛhasvāmiparigrahe /
manuṣyadhanahastyaśvapaśuvṛddhikarī bhava //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye sabhāgṛhasthāpanaṃ nāma
pañcaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 gopucchahastaka iti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 devājñāṃ prāpya iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 193
:ś atha ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sādhāraṇapratiṣṭhāvidhānaṃ
65.d:
देशस्वामिपुरस्वामिगृहस्वामिपरिग्रहे /
मनुष्यधनहस्त्यश्वपशुवृद्धिकरी भव //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये सभागृहस्थापनं नाम
पञ्चषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 गोपुच्छहस्तक इति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 देवाज्ञां प्राप्य इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 193
:श् अथ षट्षष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
साधारणप्रतिष्ठाविधानं
65.m:
In the possession of the ruler of the country, the ruler of the city, and the master of the house,
bring about the increase of men, wealth, elephants, horses, and cattle!
Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Consecration of an Assembly Hall', in the ancient Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
[...]
1. 'gopucchahastakaḥ' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked gha.
2. 'devājñāṃ prāpya' is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ga. / [Page 193]
Now the sixty-sixth chapter.
Rules for general consecration.

66.s:
bhagavānuvāca
samudāyapratiṣṭhāñca vakṣye sā vāsudevavat /
ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyā viśve 'śvinau tathā //
66.d:
भगवानुवाच
समुदायप्रतिष्ठाञ्च वक्ष्ये सा वासुदेववत् /
आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्या विश्वे ऽश्विनौ तथा //
66.m: The Lord said: / I shall explain collective consecration; it is like that of Vāsudeva: / the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Viśvedevas, and the two Aśvins,

66.s:
ṛṣayaś ca tathā sarve vakṣye teṣāṃ viśeṣakaṃ /
yasya devasya yannāma tasyādyaṃ gṛhya cākṣaraṃ //
66.d:
ऋषयश् च तथा सर्वे वक्ष्ये तेषां विशेषकं /
यस्य देवस्य यन्नाम तस्याद्यं गृह्य चाक्षरं //
66.m: and likewise all the ṛṣis—I shall state their particular rule. / Taking the first syllable of whatever is that deity's name,

66.s:
mātrābhirbhedayitvā tu dīrghāṇyaṅgāni bhedayet(1) /
prathamaṃ kalpayedvījaṃ savinduṃ praṇavaṃ natiṃ(2) //
66.d:
मात्राभिर्भेदयित्वा तु दीर्घाण्यङ्गानि भेदयेत्(1) /
प्रथमं कल्पयेद्वीजं सविन्दुं प्रणवं नतिं(2) //
66.m: and differentiating it with vowels, one should differentiate the long-vowelled limb-mantras. / First one should formulate the seed-syllable with a nasal dot, the praṇava, and an obeisance.

66.s:
sarveṣāṃ mūlamantreṇa pūjanaṃ sthāpanaṃ tathā /
niyamavratakṛcchrāṇāṃ maṭhasaṅkramaveśmanāṃ //
66.d:
सर्वेषां मूलमन्त्रेण पूजनं स्थापनं तथा /
नियमव्रतकृच्छ्राणां मठसङ्क्रमवेश्मनां //
66.m: Worship and consecration of all [deities] are done with their basic mantra. / Of restrictive observances, vows, and penances, of monasteries, bridges, and houses,

66.s:
māsopavāsaṃ dvādaśyāṃ ity ādisthāpanaṃ vade /
śilāṃ pūrṇaghaṭaṃ kāṃsyaṃ sambhāraṃ sthāpayettataḥ //
66.d:
मासोपवासं द्वादश्यां इत्य् आदिस्थापनं वदे /
शिलां पूर्णघटं कांस्यं सम्भारं स्थापयेत्ततः //
66.m: of the month-long fast ending on the twelfth lunar day—I shall explain the consecration of these and the like. / Then one should set up a stone, a full jar, bronze [vessels], and ritual paraphernalia.

66.s:
brahmakūrcaṃ samāhṛtya śraped yavamayaṃ caruṃ /
kṣīreṇa kapilāyāstu tadviṣṇoriti sādhakaḥ //
66.d:
ब्रह्मकूर्चं समाहृत्य श्रपेद् यवमयं चरुं /
क्षीरेण कपिलायास्तु तद्विष्णोरिति साधकः //
66.m: Having procured a Brahmā-bundle, the practitioner should cook a barley sacrificial boiled offering / with milk from a tawny cow, reciting 'tad viṣṇoḥ...'

66.s:
praṇavenābhighāryaiva darvyā saṅghaṭṭayettataḥ /
sādhayitvāvatāryātha viṣṇumabhyarcya homayet //
66.d:
प्रणवेनाभिघार्यैव दर्व्या सङ्घट्टयेत्ततः /
साधयित्वावतार्याथ विष्णुमभ्यर्च्य होमयेत् //
66.m: Having sprinkled it with clarified butter reciting the praṇava, he should stir it with a ladle. / Having cooked it and taken it down, and having worshipped Viṣṇu, he should make fire oblations.

66.s:
vyāhṛtā caiva gāyatryā tadviprāseti homayet /
viśvataś cakṣurvedyair bhūragnaye tathaiva ca //
66.d:
व्याहृता चैव गायत्र्या तद्विप्रासेति होमयेत् /
विश्वतश् चक्षुर्वेद्यैर् भूरग्नये तथैव च //
66.m: He should make fire oblations with the sacred utterances, the Gāyatrī, and 'tad viprāsaḥ...', / with the hymns to the all-seeing one, to the altars, and 'to Agni, Bhūḥ!' likewise,

66.s:
sūryāya prajāpataye antarikṣāya homayet /
dyauḥ svāhā brahmaṇe svāhā pṛthivī mahārājakaḥ //
66.d:
सूर्याय प्रजापतये अन्तरिक्षाय होमयेत् /
द्यौः स्वाहा ब्रह्मणे स्वाहा पृथिवी महाराजकः //
66.m: to Sūrya, to Prajāpati, and to the intermediate space he should make fire oblations: / 'To heaven, svāhā! To Brahmā, svāhā! Earth is the great king;'

66.s:
tasmai somañca rājānaṃ indrādyair homamācaret /
:n
1 aṅgāni kalpayediti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 praṇavaṃ gatimiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 194
evaṃ hutvā(1) carorbhāgān dadyāddigbalimādarāt //
66.d:
तस्मै सोमञ्च राजानं इन्द्राद्यैर् होममाचरेत् /
:न्
1 अङ्गानि कल्पयेदिति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 प्रणवं गतिमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 194
एवं हुत्वा(1) चरोर्भागान् दद्याद्दिग्बलिमादरात् //
66.m:
and he should perform the fire oblation to King Soma, and to Indra and the others.
[...]
1. 'aṅgāni kalpayet' is the reading in both manuscripts marked kha and ṅa.
2. 'praṇavaṃ gatim' is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / [Page 194]
Having offered oblations in this way, he should attentively distribute portions of the sacrificial boiled offering as offerings to the directions.

66.s:
samidho 'ṣṭaśataṃ hutvā pālāśāṃścājyahomakaṃ /
kuryāt puruṣasūktena irāvatī tilāṣṭakaṃ //
66.d:
समिधो ऽष्टशतं हुत्वा पालाशांश्चाज्यहोमकं /
कुर्यात् पुरुषसूक्तेन इरावती तिलाष्टकं //
66.m: Having offered one hundred and eight fuel-sticks of palāśa wood, he should offer clarified butter / with the Puruṣasūkta, 'irāvatī...', and eight offerings of sesame.

66.s:
hutvā tu brahmaviṣṇvīśadevānāmanuyāyināṃ /
grahāṇāmāhutīrhutvā lokeśānāmatho punaḥ //
66.d:
हुत्वा तु ब्रह्मविष्ण्वीशदेवानामनुयायिनां /
ग्रहाणामाहुतीर्हुत्वा लोकेशानामथो पुनः //
66.m: Having made oblations to the followers of the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśa, / and having offered oblations to the planets, and then further to the world-guardians,

66.s:
parvatānāṃ nadīnāñca samudrāṇāṃ tathā.ahutīḥ /
hutvā ca vyāhṛtīrdaddyāt sruvapūrṇāhutitrayaṃ //
66.d:
पर्वतानां नदीनाञ्च समुद्राणां तथा.अहुतीः /
हुत्वा च व्याहृतीर्दद्द्यात् स्रुवपूर्णाहुतित्रयं //
66.m: and having offered oblations to the mountains, rivers, and oceans, / and offered the sacred utterances, he should offer three full ladles of final oblations,

66.s:
vauṣaḍantena mantreṇa vaiṣṇavena pitāmaha /
pañcagavyaṃ caruṃ prāśya datvācāryāya dakṣiṇāṃ //
66.d:
वौषडन्तेन मन्त्रेण वैष्णवेन पितामह /
पञ्चगव्यं चरुं प्राश्य दत्वाचार्याय दक्षिणां //
66.m: with a Vaiṣṇava mantra ending in vauṣaṭ, O grandfather! / Having consumed the pañcagavya and the sacrificial boiled offering, and having given a sacrificial fee to the ācārya,

66.s:
tilapātraṃ hemayuktaṃ savastraṃ gāmalaṅkṛtāṃ /
prīyatāṃ bhagavān viṣṇurityutsṛjedvrataṃ budhaḥ //
66.d:
तिलपात्रं हेमयुक्तं सवस्त्रं गामलङ्कृतां /
प्रीयतां भगवान् विष्णुरित्युत्सृजेद्व्रतं बुधः //
66.m: a vessel of sesame accompanied by gold, and an adorned cow with a garment, / the wise man should conclude the vow, saying: 'May the Lord Viṣṇu be pleased!'

66.s:
māsopavāsāderanyāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vacmi pūrṇataḥ /
yajñenātoṣya deveśaṃ śrapayedvaiṣṇavaṃ caruṃ //
66.d:
मासोपवासादेरन्यां प्रतिष्ठां वच्मि पूर्णतः /
यज्ञेनातोष्य देवेशं श्रपयेद्वैष्णवं चरुं //
66.m: I shall state fully another consecration for the month-long fast and the like: / Having gratified the Lord of the gods with a sacrifice, he should cook a Vaiṣṇava sacrificial boiled offering

66.s:
tilataṇḍulanīvāraiḥ śyāmākair athavā yavaiḥ /
ājyenādhārya cottārya homayenmūrtimantrakaiḥ //
66.d:
तिलतण्डुलनीवारैः श्यामाकैर् अथवा यवैः /
आज्येनाधार्य चोत्तार्य होमयेन्मूर्तिमन्त्रकैः //
66.m: with sesame, unhusked rice, wild rice, millet, or barley. / Having sprinkled it with clarified butter and taken it down, he should make fire oblations with the mantras of the icon.

66.s:
viṣṇvādīnāṃ māsapānāṃ tadante homayet punaḥ /
oṃ viṣṇave svāhā / oṃ viṣṇave(2) nibhūyapāya svāhā / oṃ
viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya svāhā / oṃ narasiṃhāya svāhā / oṃ
puruṣottamāya svāhā
dvādaśāśvatthasamidho homayedghṛtasamplutāḥ //
66.d:
विष्ण्वादीनां मासपानां तदन्ते होमयेत् पुनः /
ओं विष्णवे स्वाहा / ओं विष्णवे(2) निभूयपाय स्वाहा / ओं
विष्णवे शिपिविष्टाय स्वाहा / ओं नरसिंहाय स्वाहा / ओं
पुरुषोत्तमाय स्वाहा
द्वादशाश्वत्थसमिधो होमयेद्घृतसम्प्लुताः //
66.m:
At the end of that, he should again make fire oblations to Viṣṇu and the other guardians of the months:
'Oṃ, to Viṣṇu, svāhā! Oṃ, to Viṣṇu Nibhūyapa, svāhā! Oṃ, / to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa, svāhā! Oṃ, to Narasiṃha, svāhā! Oṃ, / to Puruṣottama, svāhā!'
He should offer twelve sacred fig fuel-sticks soaked in clarified butter,

66.s:
viṣṇo rarāṭamantreṇa tato dvādaśa cāhutīḥ /
:n
1 evaṃ datvā iti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / etān datvā iti gha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 oṃ viṣṇave pravṛṣāya svāhā iti gha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 195
idaṃ viṣṇurirāvatī carordvādaśa āhutīḥ //
66.d:
विष्णो रराटमन्त्रेण ततो द्वादश चाहुतीः /
:न्
1 एवं दत्वा इति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / एतान् दत्वा इति घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 ओं विष्णवे प्रवृषाय स्वाहा इति घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 195
इदं विष्णुरिरावती चरोर्द्वादश आहुतीः //
66.m:
and then twelve oblations with the mantra 'viṣṇo rarāṭam...'
[...]
1. 'evaṃ datvā' is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha and ṅa; 'etān datvā' is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.
2. 'oṃ viṣṇave pravṛṣāya svāhā' is the reading in the manuscript marked gha. / [Page 195]
With 'idaṃ viṣṇuḥ...' and 'irāvatī...', twelve oblations of the sacrificial boiled offering.

66.s:
hutvā cājyāhutīstadvattadviprāseti homayet /
śeṣahomaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā dadyāt pūrṇāhutitrayaṃ //
66.d:
हुत्वा चाज्याहुतीस्तद्वत्तद्विप्रासेति होमयेत् /
शेषहोमं ततः कृत्वा दद्यात् पूर्णाहुतित्रयं //
66.m: Having offered oblations of clarified butter in like manner, he should offer with 'tad viprāsaḥ...' / Then, having performed the remaining fire oblations, he should make three full ladles of final oblations.

66.s:
yuñjatetyanuvākantu(1) japtvā prāśīta vai caruṃ /
praṇavena svaśabdānte kṛtvā pātre tu paippale //
66.d:
युञ्जतेत्यनुवाकन्तु(1) जप्त्वा प्राशीत वै चरुं /
प्रणवेन स्वशब्दान्ते कृत्वा पात्रे तु पैप्पले //
66.m: Having recited the section beginning with 'yuñjate...', he should indeed consume the sacrificial boiled offering, / having placed it in a vessel of sacred fig wood, with the praṇava following one's own word.

66.s:
tato māsādhipānāntu viprān dvādaśa bhojayet /
trayodaśa gurustatra tebhyo dadyāttrayodaśa //
66.d:
ततो मासाधिपानान्तु विप्रान् द्वादश भोजयेत् /
त्रयोदश गुरुस्तत्र तेभ्यो दद्यात्त्रयोदश //
66.m: Then he should feed twelve brahmins representing the lords of the months; / the guru is the thirteenth there, and to them he should give thirteen

66.s: kumbhān svādvambusaṃyuktān(2) sacchatropānahānvitān /
66.d: कुम्भान् स्वाद्वम्बुसंयुक्तान्(2) सच्छत्रोपानहान्वितान् /
66.m: jars filled with sweet water, accompanied by parasols and sandals.

66.s:
gāvaḥ prītiṃ samāyāntu pracarantu praharṣitāḥ /
iti gopathamutsṛjya yūpaṃ tatra niveśayet //
66.d:
गावः प्रीतिं समायान्तु प्रचरन्तु प्रहर्षिताः /
इति गोपथमुत्सृज्य यूपं तत्र निवेशयेत् //
66.m: 'May the cows be filled with delight, may they wander rejoicing!' / Having thus dedicated a pasture path, he should erect a sacrificial post there.

66.s:
daśahastaṃ prapā.arāmamaṭhasaṅkramaṇādiṣu /
gṛhe ca homamevantu kṛtvā sarvaṃ yathāvidhi //
66.d:
दशहस्तं प्रपा.अराममठसङ्क्रमणादिषु /
गृहे च होममेवन्तु कृत्वा सर्वं यथाविधि //
66.m: For a water booth, a pleasure grove, a monastery, a bridge, and the like, measuring ten cubits, / and for a house, having thus performed all fire oblations according to rule,

66.s:
pūrvoktena vidhānena praviśecca gṛhaṃ gṛhī /
anivāritamannādyaṃ sarveṣveteṣu kārayet //
66.d:
पूर्वोक्तेन विधानेन प्रविशेच्च गृहं गृही /
अनिवारितमन्नाद्यं सर्वेष्वेतेषु कारयेत् //
66.m: the householder should enter the house according to the previously stated ritual. / He should provide unhindered food and hospitality in all these [occasions].

66.s:
dvijebhyo dakṣiṇā deyā yathāśaktyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ /
ārāmaṃ kārayedyastu nandane sa ciraṃ vaset //
66.d:
द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणा देया यथाशक्त्या विचक्षणैः /
आरामं कारयेद्यस्तु नन्दने स चिरं वसेत् //
66.m: Sacrificial fees should be given to the twice-born by the wise according to their ability. / One who lays out a pleasure grove will dwell long in the Nandana garden.

66.s:
maṭhapradānāt svarloke śakraloke vasettataḥ /
prapādānādvāruṇena saṅkrameṇa vaseddivi //
66.d:
मठप्रदानात् स्वर्लोके शक्रलोके वसेत्ततः /
प्रपादानाद्वारुणेन सङ्क्रमेण वसेद्दिवि //
66.m: From the donation of a monastery, one dwells in heaven, and then in Indra's realm. / From the donation of a water booth, [one reaches] the realm of Varuṇa; by building a bridge, one dwells in heaven.

66.s:
iṣṭakāsetukārī ca goloke mārgakṛdgavāṃ /
niyamavratakṛdviṣṇuḥ kṛcchrakṛtsarvapāpahā //
66.d:
इष्टकासेतुकारी च गोलोके मार्गकृद्गवां /
नियमव्रतकृद्विष्णुः कृच्छ्रकृत्सर्वपापहा //
66.m: One who constructs a brick causeway and creates a path for cows [attains] the world of cows. / One who undertakes restrictive observances and vows becomes Viṣṇu; one who performs penances destroys all sins.

66.s:
gṛhaṃ datvā vasetsvarge yāvadābhūtasamplavaṃ /
:n
1 añjatetyanuvākastu iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 svādvannasaṃyuktāniti kha, ga, gha, ṅa,
cihnitapustakacatuṣṭayapāṭhaḥ
:p 196
samudāyapratiṣṭheṣṭā śivādīnāṃ gṛhātmanāṃ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye samudāyapratiṣṭhākathanaṃ nāma
ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
jīrṇoddhāravidhānaṃ
66.d:
गृहं दत्वा वसेत्स्वर्गे यावदाभूतसम्प्लवं /
:न्
1 अञ्जतेत्यनुवाकस्तु इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 स्वाद्वन्नसंयुक्तानिति ख, ग, घ, ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकचतुष्टयपाठः
:प् 196
समुदायप्रतिष्ठेष्टा शिवादीनां गृहात्मनां //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये समुदायप्रतिष्ठाकथनं नाम
षट्षष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
जीर्णोद्धारविधानं
66.m:
Having donated a house, one will dwell in heaven until the dissolution of all created beings.
[...]
1. 'añjatetyanuvākastu' is the reading in the manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.
2. 'svādvannasaṃyuktān' is the reading in the four manuscripts marked kha, ga, gha, and ṅa. / [Page 196]
Collective consecration is prescribed for Śiva and other deities residing in domestic shrines.
Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter, named 'The Exposition of Collective Consecration', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now the sixty-seventh chapter.
Rules for the restoration of the dilapidated.

67.s:
bhagavānuvāca
jīrṇāddhāravidhiṃ vakṣye bhūṣitāṃ snapayedguruḥ(1) /
acalāṃ vinyasedgehe atijīrṇāṃ parityajet //
67.d:
भगवानुवाच
जीर्णाद्धारविधिं वक्ष्ये भूषितां स्नपयेद्गुरुः(1) /
अचलां विन्यसेद्गेहे अतिजीर्णां परित्यजेत् //
67.m: The Lord said: / I shall explain the procedure for restoring the dilapidated: The guru should bathe the adorned [image]; / if it is immovable, he should set it up in the shrine; if it is extremely decayed, he should discard it.

67.s:
vyaṅgāṃ bhagnāṃ ca śailāḍhyāṃ nyasedanyāṃ ca pūrvavat /
saṃhāravidhinā tatra tattvān saṃhṛtya deśikaḥ //
67.d:
व्यङ्गां भग्नां च शैलाढ्यां न्यसेदन्यां च पूर्ववत् /
संहारविधिना तत्र तत्त्वान् संहृत्य देशिकः //
67.m: If it is mutilated, broken, or full of cracks, he should install another as before. / There, having withdrawn the elemental principles through the rite of dissolution, the spiritual preceptor,

67.s:
sahasraṃ nārasiṃhena hutvā tāmuddhared guruḥ /
dāravīṃ dārayedvahnau śailajāṃ prakṣipejjale //
67.d:
सहस्रं नारसिंहेन हुत्वा तामुद्धरेद् गुरुः /
दारवीं दारयेद्वह्नौ शैलजां प्रक्षिपेज्जले //
67.m: having offered a thousand oblations with the Nṛsiṃha mantra, the guru should remove it. / A wooden image he should burn in fire; a stone-born one he should cast into water;

67.s:
dhātujāṃ ratnajāṃ vāpi agādhe vā jale 'mbudhau /
yānamāropya jīrṇāṅgaṃ chādya vastrādinā nayet //
67.d:
धातुजां रत्नजां वापि अगाधे वा जले ऽम्बुधौ /
यानमारोप्य जीर्णाङ्गं छाद्य वस्त्रादिना नयेत् //
67.m: or one made of metal, or made of gems, into unfathomable water or the ocean. / Having placed the decayed body onto a cart and covered it with cloth and the like, he should convey it,

67.s:
vāditraiḥ prakṣipettoye gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadet /
yatpramāṇā ca yaddravyā tanmānāṃ sthāpayeddine /
kūpavāpītaḍāgāderjīrṇoddhāre mahāphalaṃ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye jīrṇoddhārakathanaṃ nāma
saptaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 bhūṣitāñca yajed gururiti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 197
:ś atha aṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yātrotsavavidhikathanaṃ
67.d:
वादित्रैः प्रक्षिपेत्तोये गुरवे दक्षिणां ददेत् /
यत्प्रमाणा च यद्द्रव्या तन्मानां स्थापयेद्दिने /
कूपवापीतडागादेर्जीर्णोद्धारे महाफलं //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये जीर्णोद्धारकथनं नाम
सप्तषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 भूषिताञ्च यजेद् गुरुरिति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 197
:श् अथ अष्टषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
यात्रोत्सवविधिकथनं
67.m:
and cast it into water to the accompaniment of musical instruments; he should give a sacrificial fee to the guru. / On the [proper] day he should install another of the same dimension and the same material. / In the restoration of dilapidated wells, reservoirs, ponds, and the like, there is great fruit.
Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, named 'The Exposition of the Restoration of the Dilapidated', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
[...]
1 'bhūṣitāñca yajed guruḥ' is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.
[Page 197]
Now, chapter sixty-eight.
Description of the rules for the procession festival.

68.s:
bhagavānuvāca
vakṣye vidhiṃ cotsavasya sthāpite tu sure caret /
tasminnabde caikarātraṃ trirātrañcāṣṭarātrakaṃ //
68.d:
भगवानुवाच
वक्ष्ये विधिं चोत्सवस्य स्थापिते तु सुरे चरेत् /
तस्मिन्नब्दे चैकरात्रं त्रिरात्रञ्चाष्टरात्रकं //
68.m:
The Lord said:
And I shall declare the rite of the festival when the deity has been established; one should perform [it]
in that year, for one night, three nights, or eight nights.

68.s:
utsavena vinā yasmāt sthāpanaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet /
ayane viṣuve cāpi śayanopavane gṛhe(1) //
68.d:
उत्सवेन विना यस्मात् स्थापनं निष्फलं भवेत् /
अयने विषुवे चापि शयनोपवने गृहे(1) //
68.m:
Since without a festival the establishment would become fruitless,
at a solstice, an equinox, at the god's lying down, in a garden, or in a house,

68.s:
kārakasyānukūle vā yātrāndevasya kārayet /
maṅgalāṅkuraropaistu gītanṛtyādivādyakaiḥ //
68.d:
कारकस्यानुकूले वा यात्रान्देवस्य कारयेत् /
मङ्गलाङ्कुररोपैस्तु गीतनृत्यादिवाद्यकैः //
68.m:
or when favourable to the sponsor, one should have the procession of the deity performed,
with the sowing of auspicious sprouts and with singing, dancing, and instrumental music.

68.s:
śarāvaghaṭikāpālīstvaṅkurārohaṇe hitāḥ /
yavāñchālīṃstilān mudgān godhūmān sitasarṣapān //
68.d:
शरावघटिकापालीस्त्वङ्कुरारोहणे हिताः /
यवाञ्छालींस्तिलान् मुद्गान् गोधूमान् सितसर्षपान् //
68.m:
Shallow dishes, small pots, and bowls are beneficial for raising sprouts;
barley, rice, sesame, mung beans, wheat, white mustard,

68.s:
kulatthamāṣaniṣpāvān kṣālayitvā tu vāpayet /
pūrvādau ca baliṃ dadyāt bhraman dīpaiḥ puraṃ niśi //
68.d:
कुलत्थमाषनिष्पावान् क्षालयित्वा तु वापयेत् /
पूर्वादौ च बलिं दद्यात् भ्रमन् दीपैः पुरं निशि //
68.m:
horsegram, black gram, and flat beans—having washed them, one should sow them.
And one should make an offering beginning in the east, wandering through the town at night with lamps,

68.s:
indrādeḥ kumudādeś ca sarvabhūtebhya eva ca /
anugacchanti te tatra pratirūpadharāḥ punaḥ //
68.d:
इन्द्रादेः कुमुदादेश् च सर्वभूतेभ्य एव च /
अनुगच्छन्ति ते तत्र प्रतिरूपधराः पुनः //
68.m:
to Indra and others, to Kumuda and others, and to all spirits.
Those who follow there, bearing forms corresponding [to the deities],

68.s:
pade pade 'śvamedhasya phalaṃ teṣāṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
āgatya devatāgāraṃ devaṃ vijñāpayed guruḥ //
68.d:
पदे पदे ऽश्वमेधस्य फलं तेषां न संशयः /
आगत्य देवतागारं देवं विज्ञापयेद् गुरुः //
68.m:
gain the fruit of a horse sacrifice at every step; of this there is no doubt.
Having come to the abode of the deity, the guru should address the deity:

68.s:
tīrthayātrā tu yā deva śvaḥ kartavyā surottama /
tasyārambhamanujñātumarhase deva sarvathā //
68.d:
तीर्थयात्रा तु या देव श्वः कर्तव्या सुरोत्तम /
तस्यारम्भमनुज्ञातुमर्हसे देव सर्वथा //
68.m:
'The procession to the sacred ford which is to be performed tomorrow, O best of gods,
deign in every way, O god, to permit its undertaking!'

68.s:
devamevantu vijñāpya tataḥ karma samārabhet(2) /
prarohaghaṭikābhyāntu vedikāṃ bhūṣitāṃ vrajet //
:n
1 śayanotthāpane gṛhe iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / śayanotthāpane
hareriti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 samācarediti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 198
68.d:
देवमेवन्तु विज्ञाप्य ततः कर्म समारभेत्(2) /
प्ररोहघटिकाभ्यान्तु वेदिकां भूषितां व्रजेत् //
:न्
1 शयनोत्थापने गृहे इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / शयनोत्थापने
हरेरिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 समाचरेदिति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 198
68.m:
Having thus petitioned the deity, he should then begin the rite;
and with the two sprout-pots he should approach the decorated altar.
[...]
1 'śayanotthāpane gṛhe' is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; 'śayanotthāpane hareḥ' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
2 'samācaret' is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
[Page 198]

68.s:
catuḥstambhāntu tanmadhye svastike pratimāṃ nyaset /
kāmyārthāṃ lekhyacitreṣu sthāpya tatrādhivāsayet //
68.d:
चतुःस्तम्भान्तु तन्मध्ये स्वस्तिके प्रतिमां न्यसेत् /
काम्यार्थां लेख्यचित्रेषु स्थाप्य तत्राधिवासयेत् //
68.m:
Having four pillars, in its middle on a svastika [diagram] he should place the image;
[or] having placed on painted cloths [an image] for the desired purpose, he should perform the preliminary consecration there.

68.s:
vaiṣṇavaiḥ saha kurvīta ghṛtābhyaṅgantu mūlataḥ /
ghṛtadhārābhiṣekaṃ vā sakalāṃ śarvarīṃ budhaḥ //
68.d:
वैष्णवैः सह कुर्वीत घृताभ्यङ्गन्तु मूलतः /
घृतधाराभिषेकं वा सकलां शर्वरीं बुधः //
68.m:
Together with the Vaiṣṇavas, the wise one should perform anointing with ghee from the base,
or a consecration by aspersion with a stream of ghee throughout the entire night.

68.s:
darpaṇaṃ darśya nīrājaṃ gītavādyaiś ca maṅgalaṃ /
vyajanaṃ pūjanaṃ dīpaṃ gandhapuṣpādibhiryajet //
68.d:
दर्पणं दर्श्य नीराजं गीतवाद्यैश् च मङ्गलं /
व्यजनं पूजनं दीपं गन्धपुष्पादिभिर्यजेत् //
68.m:
Showing a mirror, offering waving of lights and an auspicious ceremony with song and instrumental music,
fanning, worship, and lamp, he should worship with perfumes, flowers, and the like.

68.s:
haridrāmudgakāśmīraśuklacūrṇādi mūrdhni /
pratimāyāś ca bhaktānāṃ sarvatīrthaphalaṃ dhṛte //
68.d:
हरिद्रामुद्गकाश्मीरशुक्लचूर्णादि मूर्ध्नि /
प्रतिमायाश् च भक्तानां सर्वतीर्थफलं धृते //
68.m:
[When] turmeric, mung bean, saffron, white powder, and the like [are placed] on the head
of the image, the fruit of all sacred fords is obtained by the devotees.

68.s:
snāpayitvā samabhyarcya yātrāvimbaṃ rathe sthitaṃ /
nayedgurur nadīrnādaiśchatrādyai rāṣṭrapālikāḥ //
68.d:
स्नापयित्वा समभ्यर्च्य यात्राविम्बं रथे स्थितं /
नयेद्गुरुर् नदीर्नादैश्छत्राद्यै राष्ट्रपालिकाः //
68.m:
Having bathed and thoroughly worshipped the festival icon mounted on a chariot,
the guru should lead it to rivers with musical sounds, umbrellas, and the like, [accompanied by] the guardians of the realm.

68.s:
nimnagāyojanādarvāk tatra vedīntu kārayet /
vāhanādavatāryainaṃ tasyāṃ vedyānniveśayet //
68.d:
निम्नगायोजनादर्वाक् तत्र वेदीन्तु कारयेत् /
वाहनादवतार्यैनं तस्यां वेद्यान्निवेशयेत् //
68.m:
Within a yojana of the river, he should erect an altar;
having brought him down from the vehicle, he should place him upon that altar.

68.s:
caruṃ vai śrapayet tatra pāyasaṃ homayettataḥ /
abliṅgaiḥ(1) vaidikair mantraistīrthānāvāhayettataḥ //
68.d:
चरुं वै श्रपयेत् तत्र पायसं होमयेत्ततः /
अब्लिङ्गैः(1) वैदिकैर् मन्त्रैस्तीर्थानावाहयेत्ततः //
68.m:
There he should cook a sacrificial porridge, and then offer an oblation of milk-rice;
then he should invoke the sacred fords with Vedic mantras addressing the waters.

68.s:
āpo hiṣṭhopaniṣadaiḥ pūjayedarghyamukhyakaiḥ /
punardevaṃ samādāya toye kṛtvāghamarṣaṇaṃ //
68.d:
आपो हिष्ठोपनिषदैः पूजयेदर्घ्यमुख्यकैः /
पुनर्देवं समादाय तोये कृत्वाघमर्षणं //
68.m:
With the Upaniṣadic verses beginning 'āpo hi ṣṭhā', he should worship with the water offering and other principal rites;
taking the god again and performing the sin-cleansing rite in the water,

68.s:
snāyānmahājanair viprair vedyāmuttārya taṃ nyaset /
pūjayitvā tadahnā ca prāsādaṃ tu nayettataḥ /
pūjayet pāvakasthantu guruḥ syādbhuktimuktikṛt //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye devayātrotsavakathanaṃ nāma
aṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 arcikair iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 199
:ś athonasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
snānavidhānaṃ
68.d:
स्नायान्महाजनैर् विप्रैर् वेद्यामुत्तार्य तं न्यसेत् /
पूजयित्वा तदह्ना च प्रासादं तु नयेत्ततः /
पूजयेत् पावकस्थन्तु गुरुः स्याद्भुक्तिमुक्तिकृत् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये देवयात्रोत्सवकथनं नाम
अष्टषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 अर्चिकैर् इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 199
:श् अथोनसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
स्नानविधानं
68.m:
he should bathe with the leading citizens and brāhmaṇas; having raised him, he should set him on the altar.
Having worshipped him, on that very day he should bring him to the temple;
and the guru should worship him residing in the fire; he will bring worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter, entitled 'The Teaching on the Festival of the Procession of the Deity', in the ancient Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
[...]
1 'arcikaiḥ' is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
[Page 199]
Now the sixty-ninth chapter.
The rules for the sacred bath.

69.s:
agnir uvāca
brahman śṛṇu pravakṣāmi snapanotsavavistaraṃ /
prāsādasyāgrataḥ kumbhānmaṇḍape maṇḍale nyaset //
69.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ब्रह्मन् शृणु प्रवक्षामि स्नपनोत्सवविस्तरं /
प्रासादस्याग्रतः कुम्भान्मण्डपे मण्डले न्यसेत् //
69.m:
Agni said:
O brāhmaṇa, hear! I shall declare the details of the bathing festival:
In front of the temple, one should place pots in a pavilion upon a maṇḍala.

69.s:
kuryād dhyānārcanaṃ homaṃ harerādau ca karmasu /
sahasraṃ vā śataṃ vāpi homayet pūrṇayā saha //
69.d:
कुर्याद् ध्यानार्चनं होमं हरेरादौ च कर्मसु /
सहस्रं वा शतं वापि होमयेत् पूर्णया सह //
69.m:
One should perform meditation, worship, and fire oblation to Hari at the beginning of the rites;
one should make fire oblations a thousand or a hundred times along with the final full oblation.

69.s:
snānadravyāṇyathāhṛtya kalaśāṃścāpi vinyaset /
adhivāsya sūtrakaṇṭhān dhārayenmaṇḍale ghaṭān //
69.d:
स्नानद्रव्याण्यथाहृत्य कलशांश्चापि विन्यसेत् /
अधिवास्य सूत्रकण्ठान् धारयेन्मण्डले घटान् //
69.m:
Then, having fetched the bath ingredients, one should also arrange the jars;
having performed the preliminary consecration, one should set the pots with cords bound round their necks upon the maṇḍala.

69.s:
caturasraṃ puraṃ kṛtvā rudraistaṃ pravibhājyet(1) /
madhyena tu caruṃ sthāpya pārśve paṅktiṃ pramārjayet //
69.d:
चतुरस्रं पुरं कृत्वा रुद्रैस्तं प्रविभाज्येत्(1) /
मध्येन तु चरुं स्थाप्य पार्श्वे पङ्क्तिं प्रमार्जयेत् //
69.m:
Having made a square city, he should divide it by eleven;
having placed the sacrificial porridge in the centre, he should wipe the row at the side.

69.s:
śālicūrṇādināpūrya pūrvādinavakeṣu ca /
kumbhamudrāṃ tato badhvā ghaṭaṃ tatrānayed budhaḥ //
69.d:
शालिचूर्णादिनापूर्य पूर्वादिनवकेषु च /
कुम्भमुद्रां ततो बध्वा घटं तत्रानयेद् बुधः //
69.m:
Having filled it with rice flour and the like, in the groups of nine starting in the east,
then having formed the pot gesture, the wise one should bring the pot there.

69.s:
puṇḍarīkākṣamantreṇa darbhāṃstāṃstu visarjayet /
adbhiḥ pūrṇaṃ sarvaratnayutaṃ madhye nyased ghaṭaṃ //
69.d:
पुण्डरीकाक्षमन्त्रेण दर्भांस्तांस्तु विसर्जयेत् /
अद्भिः पूर्णं सर्वरत्नयुतं मध्ये न्यसेद् घटं //
69.m:
He should dismiss those darbha grasses with the mantra of the Lotus-eyed One;
he should place a pot filled with water and equipped with all gems in the centre.

69.s:
yavavrīhitilāṃś caiva nīvarān śyāmakān kramāt /
kulatthamudgasiddhārthāṃstacchuktānaṣṭadikṣu ca //
69.d:
यवव्रीहितिलांश् चैव नीवरान् श्यामकान् क्रमात् /
कुलत्थमुद्गसिद्धार्थांस्तच्छुक्तानष्टदिक्षु च //
69.m:
Barley, rice grains, sesame, wild rice, and śyāmāka grain in order,
horsegram, mung beans, and white mustard—their crushed forms in the eight directions.

69.s:
aindre tu navake madhye ghṛtapūrṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ nyaset /
palāśāśvatthanyagrodhavilvodumbaraśīrṣāṃ //
69.d:
ऐन्द्रे तु नवके मध्ये घृतपूर्णं घटं न्यसेत् /
पलाशाश्वत्थन्यग्रोधविल्वोदुम्बरशीर्षां //
69.m:
In the eastern group of nine, in the centre, he should place a pot filled with ghee;
with the tops of palāśa, aśvattha, nyagrodha, vilva, udumbara,

69.s:
jambūśamīkapitthānāṃ tvakkaṣāyair ghaṭāṣṭakaṃ /
āgneyanavake madhye madhupūrṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ nyaset //
69.d:
जम्बूशमीकपित्थानां त्वक्कषायैर् घटाष्टकं /
आग्नेयनवके मध्ये मधुपूर्णं घटं न्यसेत् //
69.m:
jambū, śamī, and kapittha bark-decoctions, eight pots [are filled];
in the south-eastern group of nine, in the centre, he should place a pot filled with honey.

69.s:
gośṛṅganaśvagaṅgāgajendradaśaneṣu ca /
tīrthakṣetrakhaleṣvaṣṭau mṛttikāḥ syurghaṭāṣṭake //
:n
1 pravibhāvayediti kha, ga, gha, cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
:p 200
69.d:
गोशृङ्गनश्वगङ्गागजेन्द्रदशनेषु च /
तीर्थक्षेत्रखलेष्वष्टौ मृत्तिकाः स्युर्घटाष्टके //
:न्
1 प्रविभावयेदिति ख, ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
:प् 200
69.m:
From the horn of a cow, a horse, the Gaṅgā, and the tusk of a lordly elephant,
and from a sacred ford, a field, and a threshing floor—these should be eight soils in eight pots.
[...]
1 'pravibhāvayet' is the reading in the three manuscripts marked kha, ga, and gha.
[Page 200]

69.s:
yāmye tu navake madhye tilatailaghaṭaṃ nyaset /
nāraṅgamatha jambīraṃ kharjūraṃ mṛdvikāṃ kramāt //
69.d:
याम्ये तु नवके मध्ये तिलतैलघटं न्यसेत् /
नारङ्गमथ जम्बीरं खर्जूरं मृद्विकां क्रमात् //
69.m:
In the southern group of nine, in the centre, he should place a pot of sesame oil;
orange, and then lime, date, grape, in order,

69.s:
nārikelaṃ nyaset pūgaṃ dāḍimaṃ panasaṃ phalaṃ /
nairṛte navake madhye kṣīrapūrṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ nyaset //
69.d:
नारिकेलं न्यसेत् पूगं दाडिमं पनसं फलं /
नैरृते नवके मध्ये क्षीरपूर्णं घटं न्यसेत् //
69.m:
coconut, betel nut, pomegranate, and jackfruit: he should deposit the fruits.
In the south-western group of nine, in the centre, he should place a pot filled with milk.

69.s:
kuṅkumaṃ nāgapuṣpañca campakaṃ mālatīṃ kramāt /
mallikāmatha punnāgaṃ karavīraṃ mahotpalaṃ //
69.d:
कुङ्कुमं नागपुष्पञ्च चम्पकं मालतीं क्रमात् /
मल्लिकामथ पुन्नागं करवीरं महोत्पलं //
69.m:
Saffron, nāgapuṣpa, campaka, and jasmine in order,
mallikā, then punnāga, oleander, and blue water lily—

69.s:
puṣpāṇi cāpye navake madhye vai nārikelakam /
nādayematha sāmudraṃ sārasaṃ kaupameva ca //
69.d:
पुष्पाणि चाप्ये नवके मध्ये वै नारिकेलकम् /
नादयेमथ सामुद्रं सारसं कौपमेव च //
69.m:
flowers; and in the western group of nine, in the centre indeed, a coconut.
River water, ocean water, lake water, and well water,

69.s:
varṣajaṃ himatoyañca nairjharaṅgāṅgameva ca /
udakānyatha vāyavye navake kadalīphalaṃ //
69.d:
वर्षजं हिमतोयञ्च नैर्झरङ्गाङ्गमेव च /
उदकान्यथ वायव्ये नवके कदलीफलं //
69.m:
rainwater, snow water, spring water, and water from the Gaṅgā:
these waters; then in the north-western group of nine, plantain fruit,

69.s:
sahadevīṃ kumārīṃ ca siṃhīṃ vyāghrīṃ tathāmṛtāṃ /
viṣṇuparṇīṃ śataśivāṃ vacāṃ divyauṣadhīrnyaset //
69.d:
सहदेवीं कुमारीं च सिंहीं व्याघ्रीं तथामृतां /
विष्णुपर्णीं शतशिवां वचां दिव्यौषधीर्न्यसेत् //
69.m:
sahadevī, kumārī, siṃhī, vyāghrī, and amṛtā,
viṣṇuparṇī, śataśivā, vacā: he should place these divine herbs.

69.s:
pūrvādau saumyanavake madhye dadhighaṭaṃ nyaset /
patramelāṃ tvacaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ bālakaṃ candanadvayaṃ //
69.d:
पूर्वादौ सौम्यनवके मध्ये दधिघटं न्यसेत् /
पत्रमेलां त्वचं कुष्ठं बालकं चन्दनद्वयं //
69.m:
Beginning in the east, in the northern group of nine, in the centre he should place a pot of curds;
patra, cardamom, cinnamon, costus, bālaka, the two types of sandalwood,

69.s:
latāṃ kastūrikāṃ caiva kṛṣṇāgurumanukramāt /
siddhadravyāṇi pūrvādau śāntitoyamathaikataḥ //
69.d:
लतां कस्तूरिकां चैव कृष्णागुरुमनुक्रमात् /
सिद्धद्रव्याणि पूर्वादौ शान्तितोयमथैकतः //
69.m:
creeper, musk, and black agarwood in succession:
these accomplished substances beginning in the east; then soothing water on one side.

69.s:
candratāraṃ kramācchuklaṃ girisāraṃ trapu nyaset /
ghanasāraṃ(1) tathā śīrṣaṃ pūrvādau ratnameva ca //
69.d:
चन्द्रतारं क्रमाच्छुक्लं गिरिसारं त्रपु न्यसेत् /
घनसारं(1) तथा शीर्षं पूर्वादौ रत्नमेव च //
69.m:
In order, he should place silver, mother-of-pearl, iron, tin,
camphor, lead, beginning in the east, and precious stones.

69.s:
ghṛtenābhyarjya codvartya snapayenmūlamantrataḥ /
gandhādyaiḥ pūjayedvahnau hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ caret //
69.d:
घृतेनाभ्यर्ज्य चोद्वर्त्य स्नपयेन्मूलमन्त्रतः /
गन्धाद्यैः पूजयेद्वह्नौ हुत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं चरेत् //
69.m: Having anointed with ghee and rubbed [the image] with fragrant paste, one should bathe it with the root mantra. / One should worship it with perfumes and other offerings, and having made fire oblations in Agni, perform the final oblation.

69.s:
baliñca sarvabhūtebhyo bhojayeddattadakṣiṇaḥ /
devaiś ca munibhirbhūpair devaṃ(2) saṃsthāpya ceśvarāḥ //
:n
1 ghoṣasāramiti kha, ga, gha, cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
2 devaiś ca munibhiḥ sārdhamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / divyaiś
ca balibhirdhūpair devamiti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 201
69.d:
बलिञ्च सर्वभूतेभ्यो भोजयेद्दत्तदक्षिणः /
देवैश् च मुनिभिर्भूपैर् देवं(2) संस्थाप्य चेश्वराः //
:न्
1 घोषसारमिति ख, ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
2 देवैश् च मुनिभिः सार्धमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / दिव्यैश्
च बलिभिर्धूपैर् देवमिति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 201
69.m:
He who has paid the sacrificial fee should present an offering of food to all beings and feed them. / By gods, sages, and kings, the god having been consecrated, the lords
[...]
1 'ghoṣasāram' is the reading in the three manuscripts marked kha, ga, and gha.
2 'devaiś ca munibhiḥ sārdham' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa; 'divyaiś ca balibhirdhūpair devam' is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.

69.s:
babhūvuḥ sthāpitvetthaṃ snapanotsavakaṃ caret /
aṣṭottarasahasreṇa ghaṭānāṃ sarvabhāg bhavet //
69.d:
बभूवुः स्थापित्वेत्थं स्नपनोत्सवकं चरेत् /
अष्टोत्तरसहस्रेण घटानां सर्वभाग् भवेत् //
69.m: they became. Having consecrated [him] in this manner, one should celebrate the festival of bathing. / With one thousand and eight pitchers, one becomes a sharer in all [merit].

69.s:
yajñāvabhṛthasnānena pūrṇasaṃsnāpanaṃ kṛtam /
gaurīlakṣmīvivāhādi cotsavaṃ snānapūrvakam //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye yajñāvabhṛtasnānaṃ nāma
ūnasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vṛkṣādipratiṣṭhākathanaṃ
69.d:
यज्ञावभृथस्नानेन पूर्णसंस्नापनं कृतम् /
गौरीलक्ष्मीविवाहादि चोत्सवं स्नानपूर्वकम् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये यज्ञावभृतस्नानं नाम
ऊनसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
वृक्षादिप्रतिष्ठाकथनं
69.m:
The complete ceremonial bath is performed by means of the ritual concluding bath of the sacrifice. / The weddings of Gaurī and Lakṣmī and other festivals are preceded by bathing.
Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Concluding Bath of the Sacrifice', in the primary Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now, the seventieth chapter.
Instruction on the consecration of trees and the like.

70.s:
bhagavānuvāca
pratiṣṭhāṃ pādapānāñca vakṣye 'haṃ bhuktimuktidāṃ /
sarvauṣadhyudakair liptān piṣṭātakavibhūṣitān //
70.d:
भगवानुवाच
प्रतिष्ठां पादपानाञ्च वक्ष्ये ऽहं भुक्तिमुक्तिदां /
सर्वौषध्युदकैर् लिप्तान् पिष्टातकविभूषितान् //
70.m: The Blessed Lord said: / I shall explain the consecration of trees, which bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation: / [the trees are] anointed with water of all herbs and adorned with fragrant powder,

70.s:
vṛkṣānmālyair alaṅkṛtya vāsobhirabhiveṣṭayet /
sūcyā sauvarṇayā kāryaṃ sarveṣāṃ karṇavedhanam //
70.d:
वृक्षान्माल्यैर् अलङ्कृत्य वासोभिरभिवेष्टयेत् /
सूच्या सौवर्णया कार्यं सर्वेषां कर्णवेधनम् //
70.m: having adorned the trees with garlands, one should wrap them with garments. / With a golden needle, the piercing of the ear must be performed for all of them.

70.s:
hemaśalākayāñjanañca vedyāntu phalasaptakam /
adhivāsayecca pratyekaṃ ghaṭān balinivedanaṃ //
70.d:
हेमशलाकयाञ्जनञ्च वेद्यान्तु फलसप्तकम् /
अधिवासयेच्च प्रत्येकं घटान् बलिनिवेदनं //
70.m: Collyrium is applied with a golden probe; and on the altar, seven fruits. / One should perform preliminary consecration individually, and offer pitchers and food-offerings.

70.s:
indrāderadhivāso 'tha homaḥ kāryo vanaspateḥ /
vṛkṣamadhyādutsṛjedgāṃ tato 'bhiṣekamantrataḥ //
70.d:
इन्द्रादेरधिवासो ऽथ होमः कार्यो वनस्पतेः /
वृक्षमध्यादुत्सृजेद्गां ततो ऽभिषेकमन्त्रतः //
70.m: Then preliminary consecration of Indra and the other [guardians] and fire oblation for the lord of the forest are to be made. / From amidst the trees one should release a cow, [and] then by means of the consecration mantra,

70.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmamantraiś ca vāruṇair maṅgalai ravaiḥ(1) /
vṛkṣavedikakumbhakaiś ca(2) snapanaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ //
70.d:
ऋग्यजुःसाममन्त्रैश् च वारुणैर् मङ्गलै रवैः(1) /
वृक्षवेदिककुम्भकैश् च(2) स्नपनं द्विजपुङ्गवाः //
70.m: with Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma mantras, with mantras to Varuṇa, and auspicious chants, / using the tree altar and pitchers, the best of the twice-born

70.s:
tarūṇāṃ yajamānasya kuryuś ca yajamānakaḥ /
bhūṣito dakṣiṇāṃ dadyādgobhūbhūṣaṇavastrakaṃ //
:n
1 vāruṇamanumirvarariti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 vṛkṣavedīśakumbhaistu iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 202
70.d:
तरूणां यजमानस्य कुर्युश् च यजमानकः /
भूषितो दक्षिणां दद्याद्गोभूभूषणवस्त्रकं //
:न्
1 वारुणमनुमिर्वररिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 वृक्षवेदीशकुम्भैस्तु इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 202
70.m:
should perform the bathing of the trees and of the patron; and the patron, / adorned, should give a sacrificial fee: a cow, land, ornaments, and cloth.
[...]
1 'vāruṇamanumirvarar' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
2 'vṛkṣavedīśakumbhaistu' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.

70.s:
kṣīreṇa bhojanaṃ dadyādyāvaddinacatuṣṭayaṃ /
homastilādyaiḥ kāryastu palāśasamidhais tathā //
70.d:
क्षीरेण भोजनं दद्याद्यावद्दिनचतुष्टयं /
होमस्तिलाद्यैः कार्यस्तु पलाशसमिधैस् तथा //
70.m: He should provide food with milk for four days. / The fire oblation should indeed be performed with sesame seeds and the like, as well as kindling sticks of palāśa.

70.s:
ācārye dviguṇaṃ dadyāt pūrvavan maṇḍapādikam /
pāpanāśaḥ parā siddhirvṛkṣārāmapratiṣṭhayā //
70.d:
आचार्ये द्विगुणं दद्यात् पूर्ववन् मण्डपादिकम् /
पापनाशः परा सिद्धिर्वृक्षारामप्रतिष्ठया //
70.m: To the preceptor he should give double. The pavilion and the rest are as before. / Destruction of sin and supreme accomplishment [are obtained] by the consecration of groves of trees.

70.s:
skandāyeśo yathā prāha pratiṣṭhādyaṃ tathā śṛṇu /
sūryeśagaṇaśaktyādeḥ parivārasya vai hareḥ //
:e ity ādimāhāpurāṇe āgneye pādapārāmapratiṣṭhākathanaṃ
nāma saptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ekasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gaṇeśapūjāvidhiḥ
70.d:
स्कन्दायेशो यथा प्राह प्रतिष्ठाद्यं तथा शृणु /
सूर्येशगणशक्त्यादेः परिवारस्य वै हरेः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमाहापुराणे आग्नेये पादपारामप्रतिष्ठाकथनं
नाम सप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ एकसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
गणेशपूजाविधिः
70.m:
Just as the Lord told Skanda, hear the consecration and other rites / of Sūrya, the Lord, the Gaṇas, the Śaktis, and others of the retinue of Hari.
Thus ends the seventieth chapter, entitled 'Instruction on the Consecration of Trees and Groves', in the primary Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now, the seventy-first chapter.
Rule for the worship of Gaṇeśa.

71.s:
aiśvara uvāca
gaṇapūjāṃ pravakṣyāmi nirvighnāmakhilārthadāṃ(1) /
gaṇāya svāhā hṛdayamekadaṃṣṭrāya vai śiraḥ //
71.d:
ऐश्वर उवाच
गणपूजां प्रवक्ष्यामि निर्विघ्नामखिलार्थदां(1) /
गणाय स्वाहा हृदयमेकदंष्ट्राय वै शिरः //
71.m: The Lord said: / I shall describe the worship of the Gaṇa [chief], free of obstacles, bestowing all desires: / 'To the Gaṇa, svāhā' is the heart; 'to the Single-tusked One' is the head;

71.s:
gajakarṇine ca(2) śikhā gajavaktrāya varma ca /
mahodarāya svadantahastāyākṣi(3) tathāstrakam //
71.d:
गजकर्णिने च(2) शिखा गजवक्त्राय वर्म च /
महोदराय स्वदन्तहस्तायाक्षि(3) तथास्त्रकम् //
71.m: 'to the Elephant-eared One' is the tuft; 'to the Elephant-faced One' is the armor; / 'to the Pot-bellied One' who holds his tusk in hand is the eye and the weapon.

71.s:
gaṇo guruḥ pādukā ca śaktyanantau ca dharmakaḥ /
mukhyāsthimaṇḍalaṃ(4) cādhaścordhvacchadanamarcayet //
71.d:
गणो गुरुः पादुका च शक्त्यनन्तौ च धर्मकः /
मुख्यास्थिमण्डलं(4) चाधश्चोर्ध्वच्छदनमर्चयेत् //
71.m: One should worship Gaṇa, the guru, the sandals, Śakti, Ananta, Dharma, / the principal circle of bones below, and the covering above.

71.s:
padmakarṇikavījāṃś ca jvālinīṃ nandayārcayet /
sūryeśā kāmarūpā ca udayā kāmavartinī //
:n
1 nirvighnāṃ pāpanāśinīmiti ga, gha,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 balakarṇine ceti kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 mahodarāye daṇḍahastāyākṣi iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 mukhyāstimaṇḍalamiti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 203
71.d:
पद्मकर्णिकवीजांश् च ज्वालिनीं नन्दयार्चयेत् /
सूर्येशा कामरूपा च उदया कामवर्तिनी //
:न्
1 निर्विघ्नां पापनाशिनीमिति ग, घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 बलकर्णिने चेति ख, ग, घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 महोदराये दण्डहस्तायाक्षि इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 मुख्यास्तिमण्डलमिति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 203
71.m:
One should worship the seed-syllables of the pericarp of the lotus, Jvālinī, and Nandā, / Sūryeśā, Kāmarūpā, Udayā, Kāmavartinī,
[...]
1 'nirvighnāṃ pāpanāśinīm' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and gha.
2 'balakarṇine ca' is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha, ga, gha, and ṅa.
3 'mahodarāye daṇḍahastāyākṣi' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
4 'mukhyāstimaṇḍalam' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ṅa.

71.s:
satyāṃ ca vighnanāśā ca āsanaṃ gandhamṛttikā /
yaṃ śoṣā raṃ ca dahanaṃ plavo laṃ vaṃ tathāmṛtam //
71.d:
सत्यां च विघ्ननाशा च आसनं गन्धमृत्तिका /
यं शोषा रं च दहनं प्लवो लं वं तथामृतम् //
71.m: Satyā, and Vighnanāśā; the seat, fragrant earth, / 'yaṃ' for drying, 'raṃ' for burning, 'laṃ' for flooding, and 'vaṃ' for nectar.

71.s:
lambodarāya vidmahe mahodarāya dhīmahi tanno dantī pracodayāt /
gaṇapatirgaṇādhipo gaṇeśo gaṇanāyakaḥ /
gaṇakrīḍo vakratuṇḍa ekadaṃṣṭro mahodaraḥ //
71.d:
लम्बोदराय विद्महे महोदराय धीमहि तन्नो दन्ती प्रचोदयात् /
गणपतिर्गणाधिपो गणेशो गणनायकः /
गणक्रीडो वक्रतुण्ड एकदंष्ट्रो महोदरः //
71.m: 'We know the pot-bellied one, we meditate upon the large-bellied one; may that tusked one impel us.' / Gaṇapati, Gaṇādhipa, Gaṇeśa, Gaṇanāyaka, / Gaṇakrīḍa, Vakratuṇḍa, Ekadaṃṣṭra, Mahodara,

71.s:
gajavaktro lambuka kṣirvikaṭo vighnanāśanaḥ(1) /
dhūmravarṇā mahendrādyāḥ pūjyā gaṇapateḥ smṛtāḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye vināyakapūjākathanaṃ nāma
ekasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvisaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
snānaviśeṣādikathanaṃ
71.d:
गजवक्त्रो लम्बुक क्षिर्विकटो विघ्ननाशनः(1) /
धूम्रवर्णा महेन्द्राद्याः पूज्या गणपतेः स्मृताः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये विनायकपूजाकथनं नाम
एकसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्विसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
स्नानविशेषादिकथनं
71.m:
Gajavaktra, Lambuka, Kṣirvikaṭa, Vighnanāśana, / Dhūmravarṇa, and Mahendra and the others are taught to be worshipped for Gaṇapati.
