Thus ends the seventy-first chapter, entitled 'Instruction on the Worship of Vināyaka', in the primary Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now, the seventy-second chapter.
Instruction on special baths and other rites.

72.s:
īśvara uvāca
vakṣyāmi skanda nityādyaṃ snānaṃ pūjāṃ pratiṣṭhayā /
khātvāsinā samuddhṛtya mṛdamaṣṭāṅgulāṃ tataḥ //
72.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
वक्ष्यामि स्कन्द नित्याद्यं स्नानं पूजां प्रतिष्ठया /
खात्वासिना समुद्धृत्य मृदमष्टाङ्गुलां ततः //
72.m: The Lord said: / I shall declare, O Skanda, the daily and other baths and the worship by consecration. / Having dug with a blade and extracted clay eight fingers deep from there,

72.s:
sarvātmanā samuddhṛtya punastenaiva pūrayet /
śirasā payasastīre nidhāyāstreṇa śodhayet(2) //
72.d:
सर्वात्मना समुद्धृत्य पुनस्तेनैव पूरयेत् /
शिरसा पयसस्तीरे निधायास्त्रेण शोधयेत्(2) //
72.m: having taken it up completely, one should fill it back with the same [earth]. / Placing it on the bank of the water by the head [mantra], one should purify it with the weapon [mantra].

72.s:
tṛṇāni śikhayoddhṛtya varmaṇā vibhajettridhā /
ekayā nābhipādāntaṃ prakṣālya punaranyayā //
72.d:
तृणानि शिखयोद्धृत्य वर्मणा विभजेत्त्रिधा /
एकया नाभिपादान्तं प्रक्षाल्य पुनरन्यया //
72.m: Having removed blades of grass with the tuft [mantra], one should divide [the clay] into three parts with the armor [mantra]. / Having washed from the navel to the feet with one part, again with another,

72.s:
astrābhilabdhayālabhya dīptayā sarvavigrahaṃ /
niruddhākṣāṇi pāṇibhyāṃ prāṇān saṃyamya vāriṇi //
72.d:
अस्त्राभिलब्धयालभ्य दीप्तया सर्वविग्रहं /
निरुद्धाक्षाणि पाणिभ्यां प्राणान् संयम्य वारिणि //
72.m: obtained with the weapon [mantra], radiant, having smeared the entire body, / having closed the eyes with the hands and restrained the vital breaths in the water,

72.s:
nimajyāsīta hṛdyastraṃ smaran kālānalaprabhaṃ /
:n
1 vighnarājaka iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 nijāstreṇa viśodhayediti kha, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 204
malasnānaṃ viśodhayetthaṃ samutthāya jalāntarāt //
72.d:
निमज्यासीत हृद्यस्त्रं स्मरन् कालानलप्रभं /
:न्
1 विघ्नराजक इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 निजास्त्रेण विशोधयेदिति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 204
मलस्नानं विशोधयेत्थं समुत्थाय जलान्तरात् //
72.m:
one should remain submerged, meditating in the heart on the weapon [mantra] resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution.
[...]
1 'vighnarājaka' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
2 'nijāstreṇa viśodhayed' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ga.
In this manner one should purify the cleansing bath. Having arisen from the water,

72.s:
astrasandhyāmupāsyātha vidhisnānaṃ samācaret /
sārasvatāditīrthānāṃ ekamaṅkuśamudrayā //
72.d:
अस्त्रसन्ध्यामुपास्याथ विधिस्नानं समाचरेत् /
सारस्वतादितीर्थानां एकमङ्कुशमुद्रया //
72.m: and having performed the twilight worship with the weapon [mantra], one should perform the prescribed ritual bath. / From sacred fords like the Sārasvata, drawing forth one with the hook gesture

72.s:
hṛdākṛṣya tathā snāpya punaḥ saṃhāramudrayā /
śeṣaṃ mṛdbhāgamādāya praviśya nābhivāriṇi //
72.d:
हृदाकृष्य तथा स्नाप्य पुनः संहारमुद्रया /
शेषं मृद्भागमादाय प्रविश्य नाभिवारिणि //
72.m: into the heart and having bathed, again with the dissolution gesture, / taking the remaining portion of clay and entering into navel-deep water,

72.s:
vāmapāṇitale kuryādbhāgatrayamudaṅmukhaḥ /
aṅgair dakṣiṇamekādyaṃ pūrvamastreṇa saptadhā //
72.d:
वामपाणितले कुर्याद्भागत्रयमुदङ्मुखः /
अङ्गैर् दक्षिणमेकाद्यं पूर्वमस्त्रेण सप्तधा //
72.m: facing north, one should make three portions on the palm of the left hand. / The right first part [one should recite over] seven times with the weapon [mantra] and the limbs;

72.s:
śivena daśadhā saumyaṃ japedbhāgatrayaṃ kramāt /
sarvadikṣu kṣipet pūrvaṃ hūṃ phaḍantaśarātmanā(1) //
72.d:
शिवेन दशधा सौम्यं जपेद्भागत्रयं क्रमात् /
सर्वदिक्षु क्षिपेत् पूर्वं हूं फडन्तशरात्मना(1) //
72.m: the northern [part] ten times with the Śiva [mantra]; one should recite over the three parts in sequence. / One should cast the first in all directions with [the mantra] ending in hūṃ phaṭ having the nature of an arrow.

72.s:
kuryācchivena saumyena śivatīrthaṃ bhujakramāt /
sarvāṅgamaṅgajaptena mūrdhādicaraṇāvadhi //
72.d:
कुर्याच्छिवेन सौम्येन शिवतीर्थं भुजक्रमात् /
सर्वाङ्गमङ्गजप्तेन मूर्धादिचरणावधि //
72.m: One should create the sacred ford of Śiva with the Śiva [mantra] on the northern side along the order of the arms. / Having smeared the whole body from the head down to the feet

72.s:
dakṣiṇena samālabhya paṭhannaṅgacatuṣṭayam /
pidhāya khāni sarvāṇi sammukhīkaraṇena ca //
72.d:
दक्षिणेन समालभ्य पठन्नङ्गचतुष्टयम् /
पिधाय खानि सर्वाणि सम्मुखीकरणेन च //
72.m: with the right [hand], reciting the four limbs with that which was consecrated by the limbs, / and having closed all the apertures with the ritual orientation gesture,

72.s:
śivaṃ smarannimajjeta hariṃ gaṅgeti vā smaran /
vauṣaḍantaṣaḍaṅgena ke kuryādabhiṣecanaṃ //
72.d:
शिवं स्मरन्निमज्जेत हरिं गङ्गेति वा स्मरन् /
वौषडन्तषडङ्गेन के कुर्यादभिषेचनं //
72.m: one should plunge, remembering Śiva, or remembering Hari, or 'Gaṅgā'. / With the six limbs ending in vauṣaṭ, one should perform consecration by aspersion upon the water.

72.s:
kumbhamātreṇa rakṣārthaṃ pūrvādau nikṣipejjalaṃ /
snātvā rajopacāreṇa sugandhāmalakādibhiḥ //
72.d:
कुम्भमात्रेण रक्षार्थं पूर्वादौ निक्षिपेज्जलं /
स्नात्वा रजोपचारेण सुगन्धामलकादिभिः //
72.m: For protection, one should throw water toward the east and other directions with a mere water-pot. / Having bathed with dust rites, fragrant myrobalan, and the like,

72.s:
snātvā cottīrya tattīrthaṃ saṃhāriṇyopasaṃharet /
athāto vidhiśuddhena saṃhitāmantritena ca //
72.d:
स्नात्वा चोत्तीर्य तत्तीर्थं संहारिण्योपसंहरेत् /
अथातो विधिशुद्धेन संहितामन्त्रितेन च //
72.m:
Having bathed and emerged from the water, he should withdraw that sacred ford using the Saṃhāriṇī [mudrā].
Next, with ashes purified by rule and consecrated with the Saṃhitā mantras,

72.s:
nivṛtyādiviśuddhena bhasmanā snānamācaret /
śirastaḥ pādaparyantaṃ hrūṃ phaḍantaśarātmanā(2) //
72.d:
निवृत्यादिविशुद्धेन भस्मना स्नानमाचरेत् /
शिरस्तः पादपर्यन्तं ह्रूं फडन्तशरात्मना(2) //
72.m:
purified by [the mantras of] Nivṛtti and the rest, he should take an ash-bath,
from head to foot, using the arrow [mantra] ending in hrūṃ phaṭ.

72.s:
tena kṛtvā malasnānaṃ vidhisnānaṃ samācaret /
:n
1 krūṃ phaḍantaśarātmanā iti kha, ṅa,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 krūṃ phaḍantaśarātmanā iti kha, ṅa,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 205
īśatatpuruṣāghoraguhyakājātasañcaraiḥ(1) //
72.d:
तेन कृत्वा मलस्नानं विधिस्नानं समाचरेत् /
:न्
1 क्रूं फडन्तशरात्मना इति ख, ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 क्रूं फडन्तशरात्मना इति ख, ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 205
ईशतत्पुरुषाघोरगुह्यकाजातसञ्चरैः(1) //
72.m:
Having performed the cleansing bath with that, he should perform the ritual bath.
[...]
[Footnote: The reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ṅa is krūṃ phaḍantaśarātmanā.]
With [mantras] moving through the Īśa, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Guhyaka (Vāmadeva), and Sadyojāta faces,
With the movements of [the mantras of] Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Guhyaka (Vāmadeva), and Sadyojāta,

72.s:
krameṇoddhūnayenmūrdhni vaktrahṛdguhyavigrahāt /
sandhyātraye niśīthe ca varṣāpūrvāvasānayoḥ //
72.d:
क्रमेणोद्धूनयेन्मूर्ध्नि वक्त्रहृद्गुह्यविग्रहात् /
सन्ध्यात्रये निशीथे च वर्षापूर्वावसानयोः //
72.m:
he should progressively dust [the ash] upon the head, face, heart, genitals, and the whole body.
At the three junctures of the day, at midnight, at the beginning and end of rain,

72.s:
suptvā bhuktvā payaḥ pītvā kṛtvā cāvaśyakādikam /
strīpunnapuṃsakaṃ śūdraṃ viḍālaśaśamūṣikam //
72.d:
सुप्त्वा भुक्त्वा पयः पीत्वा कृत्वा चावश्यकादिकम् /
स्त्रीपुन्नपुंसकं शूद्रं विडालशशमूषिकम् //
72.m:
after sleeping, eating, drinking milk, performing necessary evacuations and the like,
[or having touched] a woman, a man, a eunuch, a śūdra, a cat, a hare, or a mouse,

72.s:
snānamāgneyakaṃ spṛṣṭvā śucā vuddhūlakaṃ caret /
sūryāṃśuvarṣasamparkaiḥ prāṅmukhenordhvabāhunā //
72.d:
स्नानमाग्नेयकं स्पृष्ट्वा शुचा वुद्धूलकं चरेत् /
सूर्यांशुवर्षसम्पर्कैः प्राङ्मुखेनोर्ध्वबाहुना //
72.m:
having touched [these, he should take] a bath of fire, or dusting [with ash] for purification.
Facing east with arms raised, through contact with the sun's rays and rain,

72.s:
māhendraṃ snānamaiśena kāryaṃ saptapadāvadhi /
gosaṅghamadhyagaḥ kuryāt khurotkhātakareṇubhiḥ(2) //
72.d:
माहेन्द्रं स्नानमैशेन कार्यं सप्तपदावधि /
गोसङ्घमध्यगः कुर्यात् खुरोत्खातकरेणुभिः(2) //
72.m:
the bath of Mahendra is to be performed in the north-east up to seven steps.
Standing in the midst of a herd of cows, he should perform [a bath] with dust kicked up by their hooves.

72.s:
pāvanaṃ navamantreṇa snānantadvarmaṇāthavā /
sadyojātādibhirmantrair ambhobhirabhiṣecanam //
72.d:
पावनं नवमन्त्रेण स्नानन्तद्वर्मणाथवा /
सद्योजातादिभिर्मन्त्रैर् अम्भोभिरभिषेचनम् //
72.m:
The purifying bath [is performed] with the nine-syllable mantra, or else with the armour [mantra],
[and] aspersion with water accompanied by the mantras beginning with Sadyojāta.

72.s:
mantrasnānaṃ bhavedevaṃ vāruṇāgneyayorapi /
manasā mūlamantreṇa prāṇāyāmapuraḥsaram //
72.d:
मन्त्रस्नानं भवेदेवं वारुणाग्नेययोरपि /
मनसा मूलमन्त्रेण प्राणायामपुरःसरम् //
72.m:
Such is the mantra-bath, as also for the baths of Varuṇa and Agni.
Mental [bath is performed] with the root mantra preceded by breath-control.

72.s:
kurvīta mānasaṃ snānaṃ sarvatra vihitaṃ ca yat /
vaiṣṇavādau ca tanmantrair evaṃ snānādi kārayet //
72.d:
कुर्वीत मानसं स्नानं सर्वत्र विहितं च यत् /
वैष्णवादौ च तन्मन्त्रैर् एवं स्नानादि कारयेत् //
72.m:
One should perform the mental bath, which is prescribed everywhere.
In the Vaiṣṇava and other traditions, one should likewise perform bathing and the rest with their respective mantras.

72.s:
sandhyāvidhiṃ pravakṣyāmi mantrair bhinnaiḥ samaṃ guha /
saṃvīkṣya triḥ pivedambu brahmatīrthena śaṅkaraiḥ //
72.d:
सन्ध्याविधिं प्रवक्ष्यामि मन्त्रैर् भिन्नैः समं गुह /
संवीक्ष्य त्रिः पिवेदम्बु ब्रह्मतीर्थेन शङ्करैः //
72.m:
I shall explain the rule of the twilight worship along with the distinct mantras, O Guha.
Having looked carefully, he should sip water three times through the Brahmā-tīrtha with the Śaṅkara [mantras].

72.s:
svadhāntair ātmatattvādyaistataḥ khāni spṛśeddhṛdā /
śakalīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā prāṇāyāmena saṃsthitaḥ //
72.d:
स्वधान्तैर् आत्मतत्त्वाद्यैस्ततः खानि स्पृशेद्धृदा /
शकलीकरणं कृत्वा प्राणायामेन संस्थितः //
72.m:
Then, with [the formulas of] Ātmatattva and the others ending in svadhā, he should touch the sense apertures with the heart [mantra].
Having performed the breaking into parts, established in breath-control,

72.s:
triḥ samāvartayen mantrī manasā śivasaṃhitāṃ /
ācamya nyasya sandhyāñca brāhmīṃ prātaḥ smarennaraḥ(3) //
72.d:
त्रिः समावर्तयेन् मन्त्री मनसा शिवसंहितां /
आचम्य न्यस्य सन्ध्याञ्च ब्राह्मीं प्रातः स्मरेन्नरः(3) //
72.m:
the mantra-practitioner should mentally repeat the Śivasaṃhitā three times.
Having sipped water and deposited the twilight goddess, a man should contemplate Brāhmī in the morning:

72.s:
haṃsapadmāsanāṃ raktāṃ caturvaktrāṃ caturbhujāṃ /
:n
1 guhyakājātasaṃravair iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 tatkharotkhātareṇubhiriti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 smarettata iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 206
praskandamālinīṃ dakṣe vāme daṇḍakamaṇḍaluṃ //
72.d:
हंसपद्मासनां रक्तां चतुर्वक्त्रां चतुर्भुजां /
:न्
1 गुह्यकाजातसंरवैर् इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 तत्खरोत्खातरेणुभिरिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 स्मरेत्तत इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 206
प्रस्कन्दमालिनीं दक्षे वामे दण्डकमण्डलुं //
72.m:
seated on a swan and lotus, red, four-faced, four-armed,
[...]
[Footnote: The reading in the manuscript marked kha is guhyakājātasaṃravaiḥ.]
[Footnote: The reading in the manuscript marked kha is tatkharotkhātareṇubhiḥ.]
holding a rosary of lotus seeds in the right [hand], and a staff and water-pot in the left.
holding a sacrificial ladle and rosary on the right, and a staff and water-pot on the left.

72.s:
tārkṣyapadmāsanāṃ dhyāyenmadhyāhne vaiṣṇavīṃ sitāṃ /
śaṅkhacakradharāṃ vāme dakṣiṇe sagadābhayaṃ //
72.d:
तार्क्ष्यपद्मासनां ध्यायेन्मध्याह्ने वैष्णवीं सितां /
शङ्खचक्रधरां वामे दक्षिणे सगदाभयं //
72.m:
At midday he should meditate on Vaiṣṇavī: white, seated on Garuḍa and a lotus,
holding a conch and discus on the left, and a mace with the gesture of fearlessness on the right.

72.s:
raudrīṃ dhyāyed vṛṣābjasthāṃ trinetrāṃ śaśibhūṣitāṃ /
triśūlākṣadharāṃ dakṣe vāme sābhayaśaktikāṃ //
72.d:
रौद्रीं ध्यायेद् वृषाब्जस्थां त्रिनेत्रां शशिभूषितां /
त्रिशूलाक्षधरां दक्षे वामे साभयशक्तिकां //
72.m:
He should meditate on Raudrī [at dusk]: seated on a bull and lotus, three-eyed, adorned with the moon,
holding a trident and rosary on the right, and a spear with the gesture of fearlessness on the left.

72.s:
sākṣiṇīṃ karmaṇāṃ sandhyāṃ(1) ātmānaṃtatprabhānugaṃ /
caturthī jñāninaḥ sandhyā niśīthādau vibhāvyate //
72.d:
साक्षिणीं कर्मणां सन्ध्यां(1) आत्मानंतत्प्रभानुगं /
चतुर्थी ज्ञानिनः सन्ध्या निशीथादौ विभाव्यते //
72.m:
He should contemplate the twilight goddess as the witness of rituals, and himself as following her radiance.
The fourth twilight of the sage is meditated upon at midnight and similar times:

72.s:
hṛdbindubrahmarandhreṣu arūpā tu pare sthitā /
śivabodhaparā yā tu sā sandhyā maramocyate //
72.d:
हृद्बिन्दुब्रह्मरन्ध्रेषु अरूपा तु परे स्थिता /
शिवबोधपरा या तु सा सन्ध्या मरमोच्यते //
72.m:
formless, abiding in the supreme within the heart, the drop, and the aperture of Brahmā.
That [state] which is devoted to the consciousness of Śiva is called the supreme twilight.

72.s:
paitryaṃ mūle pradeśinyāḥ kaniṣṭhāyāḥ prajāpateḥ /
brāhmyamaṅguṣṭhamūlasthaṃ tīrthaṃ daivaṃ karāgrataḥ //
72.d:
पैत्र्यं मूले प्रदेशिन्याः कनिष्ठायाः प्रजापतेः /
ब्राह्म्यमङ्गुष्ठमूलस्थं तीर्थं दैवं कराग्रतः //
72.m:
The tīrtha of the ancestors is at the root of the forefinger, and that of Prajāpati at the little finger;
the tīrtha of Brahmā is at the root of the thumb, and that of the gods at the tips of the fingers.

72.s:
savyapāṇitale vahnestīrthaṃ somasya vāmataḥ /
ṛṣīṇāṃ tu samagreṣu aṅgulīparvasandhiṣu //
72.d:
सव्यपाणितले वह्नेस्तीर्थं सोमस्य वामतः /
ऋषीणां तु समग्रेषु अङ्गुलीपर्वसन्धिषु //
72.m:
The tīrtha of Agni is on the right palm, and that of Soma on the left;
and that of the sages is across all the finger joints.

72.s:
tataḥ śivātmakair mantraiḥ kṛtvā tīrthaṃ śivātmakaṃ /
mārjanaṃ saṃhitāmantraistattoyena samācaret //
72.d:
ततः शिवात्मकैर् मन्त्रैः कृत्वा तीर्थं शिवात्मकं /
मार्जनं संहितामन्त्रैस्तत्तोयेन समाचरेत् //
72.m:
Then, having consecrated the sacred ford in the form of Śiva with mantras identified with Śiva,
he should perform sprinkling with that water using the Saṃhitā mantras.

72.s:
vāmapāṇipatattoyayojanaṃ savyapāṇinā /
uttamāṅge kramānmantrair mārjanaṃ samudāhṛtaṃ //
72.d:
वामपाणिपतत्तोययोजनं सव्यपाणिना /
उत्तमाङ्गे क्रमान्मन्त्रैर् मार्जनं समुदाहृतं //
72.m:
The sprinkling is declared to be performed on the head successively with mantras,
applying with the right hand the water that falls into the left hand.

72.s:
nītvā tadupanāsāgraṃ dakṣapāṇipuṭasthitaṃ /
bodharūpaṃ sitaṃ toyaṃ vāmamākṛṣya stambhayet(2) //
72.d:
नीत्वा तदुपनासाग्रं दक्षपाणिपुटस्थितं /
बोधरूपं सितं तोयं वाममाकृष्य स्तम्भयेत्(2) //
72.m:
Having brought near the tip of the nose that white water embodying consciousness,
situated in the hollow of the right hand, he should draw it in through the left [nostril] and retain it.

72.s:
tatpāpaṃ kajjalābhāsampiṅgayāricya muṣṭinā /
kṣipedvajraśilāyāntu tadbhavedaghamarṣaṇaṃ //
72.d:
तत्पापं कज्जलाभासम्पिङ्गयारिच्य मुष्टिना /
क्षिपेद्वज्रशिलायान्तु तद्भवेदघमर्षणं //
72.m:
Expelling that sin resembling collyrium through the Piṅgalā [nāḍī], he should strike it
upon the thunderbolt stone with his fist; that shall be the eradication of sin.

72.s:
svāhāntaśivamantreṇa kuśapuṣpākṣatānvitaṃ /
śivāyārghyāñjalindatvā gāyatrīṃ śaktito japet //
:n
1 dākṣiṇyaḥ karmaṇāṃ sandhyā iti kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 kumbhayediti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 207
72.d:
स्वाहान्तशिवमन्त्रेण कुशपुष्पाक्षतान्वितं /
शिवायार्घ्याञ्जलिन्दत्वा गायत्रीं शक्तितो जपेत् //
:न्
1 दाक्षिण्यः कर्मणां सन्ध्या इति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 कुम्भयेदिति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 207
72.m:
With the Śiva mantra ending in svāhā, offering a handful of water offering
with kuśa grass, flowers, and unbroken grains to Śiva, he should recite the Gāyatrī according to his ability.
[...]
[Footnote: The reading in the manuscript marked kha is dākṣiṇyaḥ karmaṇāṃ sandhyā.]
I shall describe the water libation from the sacred ford of the gods according to the mantra:
One should offer water libation with 'Hauṃ to Śiva, Svāhā', and to others accompanied by Svāhā:

72.s:
tarpaṇaṃ sampravakṣyāmi devatīrthena mantrakāt /
tarpayeddhauṃ śivāyeti svāhānyān svāhayā yutān //
72.d:
तर्पणं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि देवतीर्थेन मन्त्रकात् /
तर्पयेद्धौं शिवायेति स्वाहान्यान् स्वाहया युतान् //
72.m:
I shall explain the water libation from the mantra-vessel through the tīrtha of the gods.
He should offer libation with 'hauṃ to Śiva, svāhā', and to the others with [their names] joined with svāhā:

72.s:
hrāṃ hṛdyāya hrīṃ śirase hrūṃ śikhāyai hraiṃ kavacāya /
astrāyāṣṭau devagaṇān hṛdādityebhya eva ca //
72.d:
ह्रां हृद्याय ह्रीं शिरसे ह्रूं शिखायै ह्रैं कवचाय /
अस्त्रायाष्टौ देवगणान् हृदादित्येभ्य एव च //
72.m:
'hrāṃ to the heart, hrīṃ to the head, hrūṃ to the crest-tuft, hraiṃ to the armour,
to the weapon', to the eight classes of deities, to the heart, and to the Ādityas;

72.s:
hāṃ vasubhyo 'tha rudrebhyo viśvebhyaś caiva marudbhyaḥ /
bhṛgubhyo hāmaṅgirobhya ṛṣīn kaṇṭhopavītyatha //
72.d:
हां वसुभ्यो ऽथ रुद्रेभ्यो विश्वेभ्यश् चैव मरुद्भ्यः /
भृगुभ्यो हामङ्गिरोभ्य ऋषीन् कण्ठोपवीत्यथ //
72.m:
'hāṃ to the Vasus', then to the Rudras, to the Viśvedevas, and to the Maruts,
'hāṃ to the Bhṛgus', to the Aṅgirases. Then, wearing the sacred thread around the neck, to the sages:

72.s:
atreye 'tha vasiṣṭhāya namaścātha pulastaye(1) /
kṛtave bhāradvajāya viśvāmitrāya vai namaḥ //
72.d:
अत्रेये ऽथ वसिष्ठाय नमश्चाथ पुलस्तये(1) /
कृतवे भारद्वजाय विश्वामित्राय वै नमः //
72.m:
'to Atri', then 'to Vasiṣṭha, homage', and then 'to Pulastya, homage',
'to Kratu, to Bharadvāja, indeed homage to Viśvāmitra',

72.s:
pracetase manuṣyāṃś ca sanakāya vaṣaṭ tathā /
hāṃ sanandāya vaṣaṭ sanātanāya vai vaṣaṭ //
72.d:
प्रचेतसे मनुष्यांश् च सनकाय वषट् तथा /
हां सनन्दाय वषट् सनातनाय वै वषट् //
72.m:
'to Pracetas', and to the mortals; and 'to Sanaka, vaṣaṭ',
'hāṃ to Sananda, vaṣaṭ', indeed 'to Sanātana, vaṣaṭ',

72.s:
sanatkumārāya vaṣaṭ kapilāya tathā vaṣaṭ /
pañcaśikhāya dyubhave saṃlagnakaramūlataḥ //
72.d:
सनत्कुमाराय वषट् कपिलाय तथा वषट् /
पञ्चशिखाय द्युभवे संलग्नकरमूलतः //
72.m:
'to Sanatkumāra, vaṣaṭ', likewise 'to Kapila, vaṣaṭ',
'to Pañcaśikha', to Dyubhava. From the root of the joined hands,

72.s:
sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo vauṣaṭ bhūtān devapitṝnatha /
dakṣaskandhopavītī ca kuśamūlāgratastilaiḥ //
72.d:
सर्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो वौषट् भूतान् देवपितॄनथ /
दक्षस्कन्धोपवीती च कुशमूलाग्रतस्तिलैः //
72.m:
'to all spirits, vauṣaṭ'. Then to the spirits, the gods, and the ancestors,
wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, with sesame seeds from the root and tip of the kuśa grass:

72.s:
kavyabālānalāyātha somāya ca yamāya ca /
aryamṇe cāgnisomāya varhiṣadbhyaḥ svadhāyutān //
72.d:
कव्यबालानलायाथ सोमाय च यमाय च /
अर्यम्णे चाग्निसोमाय वर्हिषद्भ्यः स्वधायुतान् //
72.m:
to Kavyavāha, to Agni, then to Soma, and to Yama,
to Aryaman, to Agni-Soma, and to the Barhiṣads, joined with svadhā;

72.s:
ājyapāya ca somāya viśeṣasuravat pitṝn /
oṃ hāṃ īśānāya pitre svadhā dadyāt pitāmahe(2) //
72.d:
आज्यपाय च सोमाय विशेषसुरवत् पितॄन् /
ओं हां ईशानाय पित्रे स्वधा दद्यात् पितामहे(2) //
72.m:
and to the Ājyapas and to Soma, to the ancestors like distinctive gods.
With 'oṃ hāṃ svadhā to Father Īśāna', he should make offerings to the grandfather,

72.s:
śāntaprapitāmahāya tathāpretapitṝṃs tathā /
pitṛbhyaḥ pitāmahebhyaḥ svadhātha prapitāmahe //
72.d:
शान्तप्रपितामहाय तथाप्रेतपितॄंस् तथा /
पितृभ्यः पितामहेभ्यः स्वधाथ प्रपितामहे //
72.m:
to the peaceful great-grandfather, and likewise to the departed ancestors;
'svadhā to the fathers, to the grandfathers', and then to the great-grandfather,

72.s:
vṛddhaprapitāmahebhyo mātṛbhyaś ca svadhā tathā /
hāṃ mātāmahebhyaḥ svadhā hāṃ pramātāmahebhyaś ca //
72.d:
वृद्धप्रपितामहेभ्यो मातृभ्यश् च स्वधा तथा /
हां मातामहेभ्यः स्वधा हां प्रमातामहेभ्यश् च //
72.m:
'to the great-great-grandfathers', and likewise 'svadhā to the mothers';
'hāṃ svadhā to the maternal grandfathers, hāṃ to the maternal great-grandfathers',

72.s:
vṛddhapramātāmahebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pitṛbhyas tathā /
:n
1 marīcaye pulastyāyeti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 hāṃ īśānāya pitre ca sadājyāya pitāmahāyeti kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 208
sarbhebhyaḥ svadhā jñātibhyaḥ sarvācāryebhya eva ca /
diśāṃ dikpatisiddhānāṃ mātṝṇāṃ graharakṣasāṃ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye snānādividhirnāma dvisaptatitamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trisaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sūryapūjāvidhiḥ
72.d:
वृद्धप्रमातामहेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पितृभ्यस् तथा /
:न्
1 मरीचये पुलस्त्यायेति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 हां ईशानाय पित्रे च सदाज्याय पितामहायेति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 208
सर्भेभ्यः स्वधा ज्ञातिभ्यः सर्वाचार्येभ्य एव च /
दिशां दिक्पतिसिद्धानां मातॄणां ग्रहरक्षसां //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये स्नानादिविधिर्नाम द्विसप्ततितमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
सूर्यपूजाविधिः
72.m:
'to the maternal great-great-grandfathers', and likewise to all the ancestors;
[...]
[Footnote: The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is marīcaye pulastyāya.]
to all relatives, Svadhā, and indeed to all teachers;
'svadhā to all kinsmen', and to all teachers,
to the directions, the guardians of the directions, the perfected beings, the Mothers, the planets, and the rākṣasas.
Thus ends the seventy-second chapter, entitled 'The Rule of Bathing and Related Rites', in the primary Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now the seventy-third chapter:
The rule for the worship of Sūrya.

73.s:
īśvara uvāca
vakṣye sūryārcanaṃ skanda karāṅganyāsapūrvakaṃ /
ahaṃ tejomayaḥ sūrya iti dhyātvārghyamarcayet //
73.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
वक्ष्ये सूर्यार्चनं स्कन्द कराङ्गन्यासपूर्वकं /
अहं तेजोमयः सूर्य इति ध्यात्वार्घ्यमर्चयेत् //
73.m:
The Lord said:
I shall explain the worship of Sūrya preceded by the ritual deposition on the hands and body, O Skanda.
Having meditated, 'I am Sūrya, consisting of fiery light', he should worship the water offering.

73.s:
pūrayedraktavarṇena lalāṭākṛṣṭavindunā /
taṃ saṃpūjya raveraṅgaiḥ kṛtvā rakṣāvaguṇṭhanaṃ //
73.d:
पूरयेद्रक्तवर्णेन ललाटाकृष्टविन्दुना /
तं संपूज्य रवेरङ्गैः कृत्वा रक्षावगुण्ठनं //
73.m:
He should fill it with red colour, with the drop drawn from the forehead.
Having worshipped him with the limbs of the Sun, and having performed the protective screening,

73.s:
samprokṣya tajjalair dravyaṃ pūrvāsyo bhānumarcayet /
oṃ aṃ hṛdvījādi(1) sarvatra pūjanaṃ daṇḍipiṅgalau //
73.d:
सम्प्रोक्ष्य तज्जलैर् द्रव्यं पूर्वास्यो भानुमर्चयेत् /
ओं अं हृद्वीजादि(1) सर्वत्र पूजनं दण्डिपिङ्गलौ //
73.m:
he should consecrate the offering substance with that water, and facing east, worship the Sun.
With 'oṃ aṃ' and the heart-seed everywhere, he should worship Daṇḍin and Piṅgala

73.s:
dvāri dakṣe vāmapārśve īśāne aṃ gaṇāya ca /
agnau guruṃ pīṭhamadhye prabhūtaṃ cāsanaṃ yajet //
73.d:
द्वारि दक्षे वामपार्श्वे ईशाने अं गणाय च /
अग्नौ गुरुं पीठमध्ये प्रभूतं चासनं यजेत् //
73.m:
at the door, on the right and left sides; in the north-east, with 'aṃ', to Gaṇa;
in the south-east to the Guru, and in the centre of the pedestal he should worship the abundant seat.

73.s:
agnyādau vimalaṃ sāramārādhyaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ /
sitaraktapītanīlavarṇān siṃhanibhān yajet //
73.d:
अग्न्यादौ विमलं सारमाराध्यं परमं सुखं /
सितरक्तपीतनीलवर्णान् सिंहनिभान् यजेत् //
73.m:
In the south-east and other directions, he should worship Vimala, Sāra, Ārādhya, and Parama Sukha,
resembling lions, colored white, red, yellow, and black.

73.s:
padmamadhye rāṃ ca dīptāṃ rīṃ sūkṣmāṃ raṃ jayāṃkramāt(2) /
rūṃ bhadrāṃ reṃ vibhūtīś ca vimalāṃ raimamoghayā //
73.d:
पद्ममध्ये रां च दीप्तां रीं सूक्ष्मां रं जयांक्रमात्(2) /
रूं भद्रां रें विभूतीश् च विमलां रैममोघया //
73.m:
In the center of the lotus [one should worship] Dīptā with *rāṃ*, Sūkṣmā with *rīṃ*, Jayā with *raṃ* in sequence,
Bhadrā with *rūṃ*, the Vibhūtis with *reṃ*, Vimalā with *raiṃ*, Amoghā with *rauṃ*,

73.s:
roṃ rauṃ vidyutā śaktiṃ pūrvādyāḥ sarvatomukhāḥ /
:n
1 oṃ hāṃ hṛdvījādīti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 ruṃ jayāṃ kramāditi kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 209
raṃ madhye arkāsanaṃ syāt sūryamūrtiṃ ṣaḍakṣaraṃ //
73.d:
रों रौं विद्युता शक्तिं पूर्वाद्याः सर्वतोमुखाः /
:न्
1 ओं हां हृद्वीजादीति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 रुं जयां क्रमादिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 209
रं मध्ये अर्कासनं स्यात् सूर्यमूर्तिं षडक्षरं //
73.m:
and Vidyut-śakti with *roṃ*, [facing] all directions starting from the east.
[Footnote]
1 *oṃ hāṃ hṛdvījādi* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2 *ruṃ jayāṃ kramāt* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / [p. 209]
With *raṃ* in the center should be the seat of the sun; the icon of Sūrya consists of six syllables.

73.s:
oṃ haṃ khaṃ kholkayeti yajedāvāhya bhāskaraṃ /
lalāṭākṛṣṭamañjalyāṃ dhyātvā raktaṃ nyasedraviṃ //
73.d:
ओं हं खं खोल्कयेति यजेदावाह्य भास्करं /
ललाटाकृष्टमञ्जल्यां ध्यात्वा रक्तं न्यसेद्रविं //
73.m:
One should worship, having invoked Bhāskara with *oṃ haṃ khaṃ kholkāya*;
having visualized the red Ravi drawn from the forehead into the folded hands, one should deposit him.

73.s:
hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ(1) sūryāya namo mudrayāvāhanādikaṃ /
vidhāya prītaye vimbamudrāṃ gandhādikaṃ dadet //
73.d:
ह्रां ह्रीं सः(1) सूर्याय नमो मुद्रयावाहनादिकं /
विधाय प्रीतये विम्बमुद्रां गन्धादिकं ददेत् //
73.m:
With *hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya namaḥ* [and] with the ritual gesture, having performed the invocation and other [rites],
one should display the circular ritual gesture for [his] pleasure and present perfume and other offerings.

73.s:
padmamudrāṃ bilvamudrāṃ pradarśyāgnau hṛdīritaṃ /
oṃ āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ arkāya śirase tathā //
73.d:
पद्ममुद्रां बिल्वमुद्रां प्रदर्श्याग्नौ हृदीरितं /
ओं आं हृदयाय नमः अर्काय शिरसे तथा //
73.m:
Having displayed the lotus gesture and the bilva gesture, [the heart mantra] is uttered in the southeast:
*oṃ āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, and likewise *arkāya śirase [namaḥ]* [in the northeast];

73.s:
bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ sureśāya śikhāyai(2) nairṛte yajet /
huṃ kavacāya(3) vāyavye hāṃ netrāyeti(4) madhyataḥ //
73.d:
भूर्भुवः स्वः सुरेशाय शिखायै(2) नैरृते यजेत् /
हुं कवचाय(3) वायव्ये हां नेत्रायेति(4) मध्यतः //
73.m:
one should worship *bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ sureśāya śikhāyai [namaḥ]* in the southwest,
*huṃ kavacāya [namaḥ]* in the northwest, [and] *hāṃ netrāya [namaḥ]* in the center.

73.s:
vaḥ astrāyeti pūrvādau tato mudrāḥ pradarśayet /
dhenumudrā hṛdādīnāṃ goviṣāṇā ca netrayoḥ //
73.d:
वः अस्त्रायेति पूर्वादौ ततो मुद्राः प्रदर्शयेत् /
धेनुमुद्रा हृदादीनां गोविषाणा च नेत्रयोः //
73.m:
*vaḥ astrāya [namaḥ]* in the east and other [cardinal directions]. Then one should display the ritual gestures:
the cow gesture for the heart and other [limbs], and the cow-horn [gesture] for the eyes.

73.s:
astrasya trāsanī yojyā grahaṇāṃ ca namaskriyā /
soṃ somaṃ buṃ budhaṃ vṛñca jīvaṃ bhaṃ bhārgavaṃ yajet //
73.d:
अस्त्रस्य त्रासनी योज्या ग्रहणां च नमस्क्रिया /
सों सोमं बुं बुधं वृञ्च जीवं भं भार्गवं यजेत् //
73.m:
The terrifying [gesture] is to be used for the weapon, and salutation to the planets:
one should worship Soma with *soṃ*, Budha with *buṃ*, Jīva with *vṛṃ*, [and] Bhārgava with *bhaṃ*,

73.s:
dale pūrvādike 'gnyādau aṃ bhaumaṃ śaṃ śanaiś caraṃ /
raṃ rāhuṃ keṃ ketave ca gandhādyaiś ca khakholkayā //
73.d:
दले पूर्वादिके ऽग्न्यादौ अं भौमं शं शनैश् चरं /
रं राहुं कें केतवे च गन्धाद्यैश् च खखोल्कया //
73.m:
on the petals starting in the east, and starting in the southeast: Bhauma with *aṃ*, Śanaiścara with *śaṃ*,
Rāhu with *raṃ*, and Ketu with *keṃ*, with perfume and the other [offerings] using *khakholkāya*.

73.s:
mūlaṃ japtvārghyapātrāmbu datvā sūryāya saṃstutiḥ /
natvā parāṅmukhañcārkaṃ(5) kṣamasveti tato vadet //
73.d:
मूलं जप्त्वार्घ्यपात्राम्बु दत्वा सूर्याय संस्तुतिः /
नत्वा पराङ्मुखञ्चार्कं(5) क्षमस्वेति ततो वदेत् //
73.m:
Having recited the root mantra and presented water from the water offering vessel to Sūrya, praise [is offered];
having bowed and turned the [vessel of the] water offering away, one should then say, 'Pardon me.'

73.s:
śarāṇunā phaḍantena samāhatyāṇusaṃhṛtiṃ(6) /
:n
1 hrīṃ hraṃ hraiṃ sa iti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 sureśāya jvāliniśikhāyai iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 krūṃ kavacāya iti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
4 hrīṃ netrāyetīti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / bhāṃ netrāyeti ga,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 parāṅmukhañcārghyamiti kha, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 śavānunā phaḍantena samāhṛtyānusaṃhatimiti kha,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ / śavāṇunā phaḍantena samahatyārthaṃ
saṃhatimiti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 210
hṛtpadme śivasūryetisaṃhāriṇyopasaṃskṛtiṃ(1) //
73.d:
शराणुना फडन्तेन समाहत्याणुसंहृतिं(6) /
:न्
1 ह्रीं ह्रं ह्रैं स इति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 सुरेशाय ज्वालिनिशिखायै इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 क्रूं कवचाय इति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
4 ह्रीं नेत्रायेतीति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / भां नेत्रायेति ग,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 पराङ्मुखञ्चार्घ्यमिति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 शवानुना फडन्तेन समाहृत्यानुसंहतिमिति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः / शवाणुना फडन्तेन समहत्यार्थं
संहतिमिति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 210
हृत्पद्मे शिवसूर्येतिसंहारिण्योपसंस्कृतिं(1) //
73.m:
Having struck [and performed] the dissolution of mantras with the arrow mantra ending in *phaṭ*,
[Footnote]
1 *hrīṃ hraṃ hraiṃ saḥ* is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.
2 *sureśāya jvāliniśikhāyai* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
3 *krūṃ kavacāya* is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ṅa.
4 *hrīṃ netrāyeti* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; *bhāṃ netrāyeti* is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
5 *parāṅmukhañcārghyam* is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha and ga.
6 *śavānunā phaḍantena samāhṛtyānusaṃhatim* is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha; *śavāṇunā phaḍantena samahatyārthaṃ saṃhatim* is the reading in the manuscript marked ga. / [p. 210]
saying 'Śiva-Sūrya' in the heart-lotus, with the withdrawal [gesture] [performing] the reabsorption,

73.s:
yojayettejaś caṇḍāya ravinirmālyamarpayet /
abhyarcyaiśe(2) japāddhyānāddhomātsarvaṃ raverbhavet //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye sūryapūjā nāma trisaptatitamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catuḥsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śivapūjākathanaṃ
73.d:
योजयेत्तेजश् चण्डाय रविनिर्माल्यमर्पयेत् /
अभ्यर्च्यैशे(2) जपाद्ध्यानाद्धोमात्सर्वं रवेर्भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये सूर्यपूजा नाम त्रिसप्ततितमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुःसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
शिवपूजाकथनं
73.m:
one should unite the brilliance into Caṇḍa and offer the sun's left-over offerings.
Having worshipped in the northeast, from recitation, visualization, and fire oblation, everything of the Sun comes to pass.
Thus ends the seventy-third chapter, named 'The Worship of Sūrya', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now the seventy-fourth chapter.
The description of the worship of Śiva.

74.s:
īśvara uvāca
śivapūjāṃ pravakṣyāmi ācamya praṇavārghyavān /
dvāramastrāmbunā prokṣya homādidvārapānyajet //
74.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
शिवपूजां प्रवक्ष्यामि आचम्य प्रणवार्घ्यवान् /
द्वारमस्त्राम्बुना प्रोक्ष्य होमादिद्वारपान्यजेत् //
74.m:
The Lord said:
I shall proclaim the worship of Śiva. Having sipped water and possessing the water offering with the praṇava,
having sprinkled the door with water consecrated by the weapon mantra, one should worship the doorkeepers starting with the southeast.

74.s:
gaṇaṃ sarasvatīṃ lakṣmīmūrdhvodumbarake yajet /
nandigaṅge dakṣiṇe 'tha sthite(3) vāmagate yajet //
74.d:
गणं सरस्वतीं लक्ष्मीमूर्ध्वोदुम्बरके यजेत् /
नन्दिगङ्गे दक्षिणे ऽथ स्थिते(3) वामगते यजेत् //
74.m:
One should worship Gaṇa, Sarasvatī, and Lakṣmī on the upper lintel;
then Nandi and Gaṅgā standing on the right, and on the left one should worship

74.s:
mahākālaṃ ca yamunāṃ divyadṛṣṭinipātitaḥ /
utsārya divyān vighnāṃś ca puṣpākṣepāntarikṣagān //
74.d:
महाकालं च यमुनां दिव्यदृष्टिनिपातितः /
उत्सार्य दिव्यान् विघ्नांश् च पुष्पाक्षेपान्तरिक्षगान् //
74.m:
Mahākāla and Yamunā. Cast down by a divine gaze,
having expelled divine obstacles, and those moving in the intermediate space by throwing flowers,

74.s:
dakṣapārṣṇitribhirghātaibhūmiṣṭhānyāgamandiraṃ /
dehalīṃ laṅghayedvāmaśākhāmāśritya vai viśet //
74.d:
दक्षपार्ष्णित्रिभिर्घातैभूमिष्ठान्यागमन्दिरं /
देहलीं लङ्घयेद्वामशाखामाश्रित्य वै विशेत् //
74.m:
[and] those on the earth by three strikes of the right heel, [approaching] the temple,
one should cross over the threshold and indeed enter leaning on the left doorpost.

74.s:
praviśya dakṣapādena vinyasyāstramudumbare /
oṃ hāṃ vāstvadhipataye brahmaṇe madhyato yajet //
:n
1 saṃhāriṇyopasaṃhatamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ /
saṃhāriṣṇopasaṃhṛtamiti ga, ṅa,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 abhyarcya ceti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 dakṣaśākhāsthite iti gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 211
74.d:
प्रविश्य दक्षपादेन विन्यस्यास्त्रमुदुम्बरे /
ओं हां वास्त्वधिपतये ब्रह्मणे मध्यतो यजेत् //
:न्
1 संहारिण्योपसंहतमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः /
संहारिष्णोपसंहृतमिति ग, ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 अभ्यर्च्य चेति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 दक्षशाखास्थिते इति घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 211
74.m:
Having entered with the right foot and placed the weapon [mantra] upon the lintel,
one should worship Brahmā, the lord of the site architecture, in the center with *oṃ hāṃ vāstvadhipataye brahmaṇe*.
[Footnote]
1 *saṃhāriṇyopasaṃhatam* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
*saṃhāriṣṇopasaṃhṛtam* is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.
2 *abhyarcya ca* is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
3 *dakṣaśākhāsthite* is the reading in the two manuscripts marked gha and ṅa. / [p. 211]

74.s:
nirīkṣaṇādibhiḥ śastraiḥ śuddhānādāya gaḍḍukān(1) /
labdhānujñaḥ śivānmaunī gaṅgādikamanuvrajet //
74.d:
निरीक्षणादिभिः शस्त्रैः शुद्धानादाय गड्डुकान्(1) /
लब्धानुज्ञः शिवान्मौनी गङ्गादिकमनुव्रजेत् //
74.m:
Taking water-pots purified with weapons such as the gaze [of inspection],
having obtained permission from Śiva, [and] remaining silent, one should walk along toward the Gaṅgā or other [waters].

74.s:
pavitrāṅgaḥ prajaptena vastrapūtena vāriṇā /
pūrayedambudhau tāṃstān gayatryā hṛdayena vā //
74.d:
पवित्राङ्गः प्रजप्तेन वस्त्रपूतेन वारिणा /
पूरयेदम्बुधौ तांस्तान् गयत्र्या हृदयेन वा //
74.m:
With limbs purified, with water consecrated by recitation and filtered through cloth,
one should fill those respective [vessels] in the reservoir with the Gāyatrī or with the heart mantra.

74.s:
gandhakākṣata(2) puṣpādisarvadravyasamuccayaṃ /
sannidhīkṛtya pūjārthaṃ bhūtaśuddhādi kārayet //
74.d:
गन्धकाक्षत(2) पुष्पादिसर्वद्रव्यसमुच्चयं /
सन्निधीकृत्य पूजार्थं भूतशुद्धादि कारयेत् //
74.m:
Having assembled all the materials—perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, and the rest—
and brought them near for the purpose of worship, one should perform the purification of the elements and other rites.

74.s:
devadakṣe tato nyasya saumyāsyaś ca śarīrataḥ(3) /
saṃhāramudrayādāya mūrdhni mantreṇa(4) dhārayet //
74.d:
देवदक्षे ततो न्यस्य सौम्यास्यश् च शरीरतः(3) /
संहारमुद्रयादाय मूर्ध्नि मन्त्रेण(4) धारयेत् //
74.m:
Then, depositing [them] to the right of the deity, facing north, from the body
taking [the soul] with the ritual gesture of withdrawal, one should hold it on the crown of the head with the mantra.

74.s:
bhogyakarmopabhogārthaṃ pāṇikacchapikākhyayā /
hṛdambuje nijātmānaṃ dvādaśāntapade 'thavā //
74.d:
भोग्यकर्मोपभोगार्थं पाणिकच्छपिकाख्यया /
हृदम्बुजे निजात्मानं द्वादशान्तपदे ऽथवा //
74.m:
For the sake of experiencing the karma to be enjoyed, with [the gesture] called the tortoise-hand,
[one should deposit] one's own self in the lotus of the heart or in the place of the twelve-finger breadth.

74.s:
śodhayet pañcabhūtāni sañcintya śuṣirantanau(5) /
caraṇāṅguṣṭhayoryugmān śuṣirāntarvahiḥ smaret //
74.d:
शोधयेत् पञ्चभूतानि सञ्चिन्त्य शुषिरन्तनौ(5) /
चरणाङ्गुष्ठयोर्युग्मान् शुषिरान्तर्वहिः स्मरेत् //
74.m:
One should purify the five elements, contemplating the hollow in the body;
from the pair of big toes of the feet, one should meditate inside and outside the hollow.

74.s:
śaktiṃ hṛdvyāpinīṃ paścāddhūṅkāre(6) pāvakaprabhe /
randhramadhyasthite(7) kṛtvā prāṇarodhaṃ hi cintakaḥ //
74.d:
शक्तिं हृद्व्यापिनीं पश्चाद्धूङ्कारे(6) पावकप्रभे /
रन्ध्रमध्यस्थिते(7) कृत्वा प्राणरोधं हि चिन्तकः //
74.m:
Then, placing the power pervading the heart into the sound *hūṃ* shining like fire
and situated in the middle of the aperture, the meditator, having restrained the breath,

74.s:
niveśayedrecakānte(8) phaḍantenātha tena ca /
hṛtkaṇṭhatālubhrūmadhyabrahmarandhre vibhidya ca //
:n
1 gandhakān iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / luḍḍukāniti kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 guḍḍukākṣateti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ /
gaṇḍūkākṣateti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 saumyāsyaḥ svaśarīrata iti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 mūrtimantreṇeti ga, gha, ṅa, cihinitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
5 svaśirastanau iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 paścādoṅkāre iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
7 candramadhyasthite iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ cakramadhyasthite iti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
8 nivodhayedrecakānte iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 212
74.d:
निवेशयेद्रेचकान्ते(8) फडन्तेनाथ तेन च /
हृत्कण्ठतालुभ्रूमध्यब्रह्मरन्ध्रे विभिद्य च //
:न्
1 गन्धकान् इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / लुड्डुकानिति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गुड्डुकाक्षतेति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः /
गण्डूकाक्षतेति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 सौम्यास्यः स्वशरीरत इति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 मूर्तिमन्त्रेणेति ग, घ, ङ, चिहिनितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
5 स्वशिरस्तनौ इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 पश्चादोङ्कारे इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
7 चन्द्रमध्यस्थिते इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः चक्रमध्यस्थिते इति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
8 निवोधयेद्रेचकान्ते इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 212
74.m:
should introduce it at the end of exhalation with [the mantra] ending in *phaṭ*, and with that,
piercing through the heart, throat, palate, eyebrow-center, and the brahmarandhra,
[Footnote]
1 *gandhakān* is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa; *luḍḍukān* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2 *guḍḍukākṣata* is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
*gaṇḍūkākṣata* is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.
3 *saumyāsyaḥ svaśarīrataḥ* is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.
4 *mūrtimantreṇa* is the reading in the three manuscripts marked ga, gha, and ṅa.
5 *svaśirastanau* is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
6 *paścādoṅkāre* is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
7 *candramadhyasthite* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; *cakramadhyasthite* is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
8 *nivodhayedrecakānte* is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / [p. 212]

74.s:
granthīnnirbhidya hūṅkāraṃ mūrdhni vinyasya jīvanaṃ /
sampuṭaṃ hṛdayenātha pūrakāhitacetanaṃ //
74.d:
ग्रन्थीन्निर्भिद्य हूङ्कारं मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्य जीवनं /
सम्पुटं हृदयेनाथ पूरकाहितचेतनं //
74.m:
having broken through the knots and deposited the vitalizing syllable *hūṃ* upon the head,
enclosed then by the heart mantra, with consciousness established by inhalation,

74.s:
hūṃ śikhopari vinyasya śuddhaṃ vindvātmakaṃ(1) smaret /
kṛtvātha kumbhakaṃ śambhau ekodghātena yojayet //
74.d:
हूं शिखोपरि विन्यस्य शुद्धं विन्द्वात्मकं(1) स्मरेत् /
कृत्वाथ कुम्भकं शम्भौ एकोद्घातेन योजयेत् //
74.m:
depositing hūṃ above the crest, one should meditate on the pure [soul] of the nature of the bindu;
then, having performed breath-retention, one should unite it with Śambhu in a single upward exertion.

74.s:
recakena vījavṛttyā śive līno 'tha śodhayet /
pratilomaṃ svadehe tu(2) vindvantaṃ tatra vindukaṃ //
74.d:
रेचकेन वीजवृत्त्या शिवे लीनो ऽथ शोधयेत् /
प्रतिलोमं स्वदेहे तु(2) विन्द्वन्तं तत्र विन्दुकं //
74.m:
by exhalation through the repetition of the seed-syllable, absorbed in Śiva, one should then purify;
in reverse order in one's own body up to the bindu, there [at the bindu]

74.s:
layannītvā mahīvātau jalavahnī parasparaṃ /
dvau dvau sādhyau tathākāśamavirodhena tacchṛṇu //
74.d:
लयन्नीत्वा महीवातौ जलवह्नी परस्परं /
द्वौ द्वौ साध्यौ तथाकाशमविरोधेन तच्छृणु //
74.m:
bringing dissolution mutually between earth and wind, water and fire,
the two pairs to be effected, and likewise space without contradiction—hear that:

74.s:
pārthivaṃ maṇḍalaṃ pītaṃ kaṭhinaṃ vajralāñchitaṃ /
haumityātmīyavījena(3) tannivṛttikalāmayaṃ //
74.d:
पार्थिवं मण्डलं पीतं कठिनं वज्रलाञ्छितं /
हौमित्यात्मीयवीजेन(3) तन्निवृत्तिकलामयं //
74.m:
the earthen maṇḍala is yellow, hard, and marked with a vajra;
with its own seed-syllable *hauṃ*, it consists of the energy of cessation.

74.s:
padādārabhya mūrdhānaṃ vicintya caturasrakaṃ /
udghātapañcakenaiva vāyubhūtaṃ vicintayet //
74.d:
पदादारभ्य मूर्धानं विचिन्त्य चतुरस्रकं /
उद्घातपञ्चकेनैव वायुभूतं विचिन्तयेत् //
74.m: Starting from the feet up to the crown, having visualized a square [maṇḍala], / one should visualize the element of wind by means of five breath-expulsions.

74.s:
ardhacandraṃ dravaṃ saumyaṃ śubhrasambhojalāñchitaṃ(4) /
hrīmityanena vījena pratiṣṭhārūpatāṃ gataṃ //
74.d:
अर्धचन्द्रं द्रवं सौम्यं शुभ्रसम्भोजलाञ्छितं(4) /
ह्रीमित्यनेन वीजेन प्रतिष्ठारूपतां गतं //
74.m: A liquid, gentle crescent, marked with a white lotus, / which has assumed the form of the [Kalā] Pratiṣṭhā through the seed-syllable 'hrīm';

74.s:
saṃyuktaṃ rāmamantreṇa(5) puruṣāntamakāraṇaṃ /
arghyañcaturbhirudghātair vahnibhūtaṃ viśodhayet //
74.d:
संयुक्तं राममन्त्रेण(5) पुरुषान्तमकारणं /
अर्घ्यञ्चतुर्भिरुद्घातैर् वह्निभूतं विशोधयेत् //
74.m: accompanied by the Vāma mantra, ending at the Puruṣa, causeless, / with four breath-expulsions, one should purify the offering of the element of fire.

74.s:
āgneyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tryastraṃ raktaṃ svastikalāñchitaṃ /
hūmityanena vījena vidyārūpaṃ vibhāvayet //
74.d:
आग्नेयं मण्डलं त्र्यस्त्रं रक्तं स्वस्तिकलाञ्छितं /
हूमित्यनेन वीजेन विद्यारूपं विभावयेत् //
74.m: The triangular fire-maṇḍala is red, marked with a svastika; / one should visualize it as the form of Vidyā through the seed-syllable 'hūm'.

74.s:
ghorāṇutribhirudghātair jalabhūtaṃ viśodhayet /
:n
1 viṣṇvātmakamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 svahetau tu iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 haumityunnīya vījeneti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ /
haumityāgneyavījeneti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 ardhacandraṃ tataḥ saumye śivaṃ pūrveṇa yojayediti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 vāmaṃ mantreṇeti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / vā samantreṇeti kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 213
ṣaḍasraṃ maṇḍalaṃ vāyorvindubhiḥ ṣaḍbhiraṅkitaṃ //
74.d:
घोराणुत्रिभिरुद्घातैर् जलभूतं विशोधयेत् /
:न्
1 विष्ण्वात्मकमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 स्वहेतौ तु इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 हौमित्युन्नीय वीजेनेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः /
हौमित्याग्नेयवीजेनेति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 अर्धचन्द्रं ततः सौम्ये शिवं पूर्वेण योजयेदिति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 वामं मन्त्रेणेति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / वा समन्त्रेणेति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 213
षडस्रं मण्डलं वायोर्विन्दुभिः षड्भिरङ्कितं //
74.m:
With the Aghora mantra and three breath-expulsions, one should purify the element of water.
[Gap in text]
[Footnote 1: "viṣṇvātmakam" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.]
[Footnote 2: "svahetau tu" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.]
[Footnote 3: "haumityunnīya vījena" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha;
"haumityāgneyavījena" is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.]
[Footnote 4: "ardhacandraṃ tataḥ saumye śivaṃ pūrveṇa yojayet" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.]
[Footnote 5: "vāmaṃ mantreṇa" is the reading in the manuscript marked gha; "vā samantreṇa" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / Page 213]
The six-angled maṇḍala of wind is marked with six dots,

74.s:
kṛṣṇaṃ hremiti vījena jātaṃ śāntikalāmayaṃ /
sañcityodghātayugmena pṛthvībhūtaṃ viśodhayet //
74.d:
कृष्णं ह्रेमिति वीजेन जातं शान्तिकलामयं /
सञ्चित्योद्घातयुग्मेन पृथ्वीभूतं विशोधयेत् //
74.m: black, produced from the seed-syllable 'hrem', consisting of the Kalā Śānti; / meditating [upon it], with two breath-expulsions, one should purify the earth element.

74.s:
nabhovindumayaṃ vṛttaṃ vinduśaktivibhūṣitaṃ /
vyomākāraṃ suvṛttañca śuddhasphaṭikanirmalaṃ //
74.d:
नभोविन्दुमयं वृत्तं विन्दुशक्तिविभूषितं /
व्योमाकारं सुवृत्तञ्च शुद्धस्फटिकनिर्मलं //
74.m: The circular [maṇḍala] of ether consists of the bindu, adorned with the power of the bindu; / having the form of the sky, well-rounded, spotless as pure crystal,

74.s:
hauṅkāreṇa phaḍantena śāntyatītakalāmayaṃ /
dhyātvaikodghātayogena suviśuddhaṃ vibhāvayet //
74.d:
हौङ्कारेण फडन्तेन शान्त्यतीतकलामयं /
ध्यात्वैकोद्घातयोगेन सुविशुद्धं विभावयेत् //
74.m: consisting of the Kalā Śāntyatīta, through the syllable 'hauṃ' ending with 'phaṭ'; / having meditated [upon it], with a single breath-expulsion, one should visualize it as thoroughly pure.

74.s:
āpyāyayettataḥ sarvaṃ mūlenāmṛtavarṣiṇā(1) /
ādhārākhyāmanantañca dharmajñānādipaṅkajaṃ //
74.d:
आप्याययेत्ततः सर्वं मूलेनामृतवर्षिणा(1) /
आधाराख्यामनन्तञ्च धर्मज्ञानादिपङ्कजं //
74.m: Then, one should refresh everything with the root mantra showering nectar: / the lotus named the support (ādhāra), Ananta, dharma, knowledge, and the rest.

74.s:
hṛdāsanamidaṃ(2) dhyātvā mūrtimāvāhayettataḥ /
sṛṣṭyā śivamayaṃ tasyāmātmānaṃ dvādaśāntataḥ //
74.d:
हृदासनमिदं(2) ध्यात्वा मूर्तिमावाहयेत्ततः /
सृष्ट्या शिवमयं तस्यामात्मानं द्वादशान्ततः //
74.m: Having meditated on this seat in the heart, one should then invoke the icon; / by way of creation, [one brings] the self, consisting of Śiva, into it from the dvādaśānta.

74.s:
atha tāṃ śaktimantreṇa vauṣaḍantena sarvataḥ /
divyāmṛtena samplāvya kurvīta sakalīkṛtaṃ //
74.d:
अथ तां शक्तिमन्त्रेण वौषडन्तेन सर्वतः /
दिव्यामृतेन सम्प्लाव्य कुर्वीत सकलीकृतं //
74.m: Then, having flooded that [icon] everywhere with divine nectar / using the Śakti mantra ending with 'vauṣaṭ', one should make it embodied (sakalīkṛta).

74.s:
hṛdayādikarānteṣu(3) kaniṣṭhādyaṅgulīṣu ca /
hṛdādimantravinyāsaḥ sakalīkaraṇaṃ mataṃ //
74.d:
हृदयादिकरान्तेषु(3) कनिष्ठाद्यङ्गुलीषु च /
हृदादिमन्त्रविन्यासः सकलीकरणं मतं //
74.m: The deposition of the heart and other mantras upon the hands ending from the heart, / and upon the fingers beginning with the little finger, is considered embodiment (sakalīkaraṇa).

74.s:
astreṇa rakṣya prākāraṃ tanmantreṇātha tadvahiḥ /
śaktijālamadhaścordhvaṃ mahāmudrāṃ pradarśayet //
74.d:
अस्त्रेण रक्ष्य प्राकारं तन्मन्त्रेणाथ तद्वहिः /
शक्तिजालमधश्चोर्ध्वं महामुद्रां प्रदर्शयेत् //
74.m: Having protected the rampart with the Astra mantra, and then, with its mantra, the net of Śakti / outside of it, below and above, one should display the great ritual gesture (mahāmudrā).

74.s:
āpadamastakaṃ yāvad bhāvapuṣpaiḥ(4) śivaṃ hṛdi /
padme yajet pūrakeṇa ākṛṣṭāmṛtasadghṛtaiḥ //
74.d:
आपदमस्तकं यावद् भावपुष्पैः(4) शिवं हृदि /
पद्मे यजेत् पूरकेण आकृष्टामृतसद्घृतैः //
74.m: From foot up to head, with the flowers of inner disposition, one should worship Śiva / in the heart-lotus with genuine clarified butter that is nectar drawn in through inhalation (pūraka).

74.s:
śivamantrair nābhikuṇḍe tarpayeta śivānalaṃ /
:n
1 mūlenāmṛtasecanāditi ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 hṛdyāsanamidamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 hṛdayādiṣaḍaṅgena iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 tāvat puṣpair iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 214
lalāṭe vindurūpañca cintayecchubhavigrahaṃ(1) //
74.d:
शिवमन्त्रैर् नाभिकुण्डे तर्पयेत शिवानलं /
:न्
1 मूलेनामृतसेचनादिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 हृद्यासनमिदमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 हृदयादिषडङ्गेन इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 तावत् पुष्पैर् इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 214
ललाटे विन्दुरूपञ्च चिन्तयेच्छुभविग्रहं(1) //
74.m:
With Śiva mantras, one should satiate the fire of Śiva in the fire-pit of the navel.
[Gap in text]
[Footnote 1: "mūlenāmṛtasecanāt" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.]
[Footnote 2: "hṛdyāsanamidam" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.]
[Footnote 3: "hṛdayādiṣaḍaṅgena" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.]
[Footnote 4: "tāvat puṣpair" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa. / Page 214]
And on the forehead, one should contemplate the bindu-formed auspicious body.

74.s:
ekaṃ svarṇādipātrāṇāṃ pātramastrāmbuśodhitaṃ /
vinduprasūtapīyūṣarūpatoyākṣatādinā //
74.d:
एकं स्वर्णादिपात्राणां पात्रमस्त्राम्बुशोधितं /
विन्दुप्रसूतपीयूषरूपतोयाक्षतादिना //
74.m: One vessel among golden vessels and the like, purified with Astra water, / with water and unbroken grains having the form of nectar produced from the bindu,

74.s:
hṛdāpūrya ṣaḍaṅgena pūjayitvābhimantrayet /
saṃrakṣya heti mantreṇa kavacena viguṇṭhayet //
74.d:
हृदापूर्य षडङ्गेन पूजयित्वाभिमन्त्रयेत् /
संरक्ष्य हेति मन्त्रेण कवचेन विगुण्ठयेत् //
74.m: having filled with the Hṛdaya mantra and worshipped with the six limbs, one should consecrate with mantras; / having protected it with the weapon mantra (heti), one should veil it with the Kavaca.

74.s:
racayitvārghyamaṣṭāṅgaṃ secayeddhenumudrayā(2) /
abhiṣiñcedathātmānaṃ mūrdhni tattoyavindunā //
74.d:
रचयित्वार्घ्यमष्टाङ्गं सेचयेद्धेनुमुद्रया(2) /
अभिषिञ्चेदथात्मानं मूर्ध्नि तत्तोयविन्दुना //
74.m: Having prepared the eight-limbed water offering, one should sprinkle it with the cow gesture (dhenumudrā); / then one should consecrate oneself on the head with a drop of that water.

74.s:
tatrasthaṃ yāgasambhāraṃ prokṣayedastravāriṇā /
abhimantrya hṛdā piṇḍaistanutrāṇena veṣṭayet //
74.d:
तत्रस्थं यागसम्भारं प्रोक्षयेदस्त्रवारिणा /
अभिमन्त्र्य हृदा पिण्डैस्तनुत्राणेन वेष्टयेत् //
74.m: One should sprinkle the sacrificial apparatus placed there with Astra water; / having consecrated [them] with the Hṛdaya mantra, one should encompass the lumps with the armour [mantra].

74.s:
darśayitvāmṛtāṃ mudrāṃ puṣpaṃ datvā nijāsane /
vidhāya tilakaṃ mūrdhni puṣpaṃ mūlena yojayet //
74.d:
दर्शयित्वामृतां मुद्रां पुष्पं दत्वा निजासने /
विधाय तिलकं मूर्ध्नि पुष्पं मूलेन योजयेत् //
74.m: Having displayed the nectar gesture (amṛtāmudrā) and placed a flower on one's own seat, / having made a tilaka mark on the forehead, one should apply a flower with the root mantra.

74.s:
snāne devārcane home bhojane yāgayogayoḥ /
āvaśyake jape dhīraḥ sadā vācaṃyamo bhavet //
74.d:
स्नाने देवार्चने होमे भोजने यागयोगयोः /
आवश्यके जपे धीरः सदा वाचंयमो भवेत् //
74.m: During bathing, deity worship, fire oblation, eating, sacrificial rite, and yoga, / and during necessary recitation, the wise person should always remain silent.

74.s:
nādāntoccāraṇānmantraṃ śodhayitvā susaṃskṛtaṃ /
pūjane 'bhyarcya gāyatryā sāmānyārghyamupāharet //
74.d:
नादान्तोच्चारणान्मन्त्रं शोधयित्वा सुसंस्कृतं /
पूजने ऽभ्यर्च्य गायत्र्या सामान्यार्घ्यमुपाहरेत् //
74.m: Having purified the mantra by uttering it up to the end of nāda, making it well consecrated, / having worshipped with the gāyatrī in the rite, one should present the general water offering.

74.s:
brahmapañcakamāvartya mālyamādāya liṅgataḥ /
aiśānyāndiśi caṇḍāya hṛdayena nivedayet //
74.d:
ब्रह्मपञ्चकमावर्त्य माल्यमादाय लिङ्गतः /
ऐशान्यान्दिशि चण्डाय हृदयेन निवेदयेत् //
74.m: Having recited the group of five Brahma mantras and taken the garland from the liṅga, / one should offer it to Caṇḍa in the northeast direction with the Hṛdaya mantra.

74.s:
prakṣālya piṇdikāliṅge astratoye tato hṛdā /
arghyapātrāmbunā siñcediti liṅgaviśodhanaṃ //
74.d:
प्रक्षाल्य पिण्दिकालिङ्गे अस्त्रतोये ततो हृदा /
अर्घ्यपात्राम्बुना सिञ्चेदिति लिङ्गविशोधनं //
74.m: Having washed the pedestal and liṅga with Astra water, then with the Hṛdaya mantra / one should sprinkle [them] with the water of the arghya vessel; this is the purification of the liṅga.

74.s:
ātamadravyamantraliṅgaśuddhau sarvān surānyajet /
vāyavye gaṇapataye hāṃ gurubhyo 'rcayecchive //
:n
1 cintayet saparigrahamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 rocayeddhenumudrayeti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 215
74.d:
आतमद्रव्यमन्त्रलिङ्गशुद्धौ सर्वान् सुरान्यजेत् /
वायव्ये गणपतये हां गुरुभ्यो ऽर्चयेच्छिवे //
:न्
1 चिन्तयेत् सपरिग्रहमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 रोचयेद्धेनुमुद्रयेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 215
74.m:
When the self, materials, mantras, and liṅga are purified, one should worship all the gods: / to Gaṇapati in the northwest, [and with] 'hāṃ' to the gurus, one should worship in Śiva.
[Gap in text]
[Footnote 1: "cintayet saparigraham" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.]
[Footnote 2: "rocayeddhenumudrayā" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / Page 215]

74.s:
ādhāraśaktimaṅkuranibhāṃ kūrmaśilāsthitāṃ /
yajed brahmaśilārūḍhaṃ śivasyānantamāsanaṃ //
74.d:
आधारशक्तिमङ्कुरनिभां कूर्मशिलास्थितां /
यजेद् ब्रह्मशिलारूढं शिवस्यानन्तमासनं //
74.m: One should worship the support-power (ādhāraśakti) resembling a sprout, resting on the tortoise-stone; / one should worship the infinite seat of Śiva, mounted upon the Brahma stone;

74.s:
vicitrakeśaprakhyānamanyonyaṃ pṛṣṭadarśinaḥ /
kṛtatretādirūpeṇa śivasyāsanapādukāṃ //
74.d:
विचित्रकेशप्रख्यानमन्योन्यं पृष्टदर्शिनः /
कृतत्रेतादिरूपेण शिवस्यासनपादुकां //
74.m: which resembles varied manes, [the lions] facing each other's backs, / in the form of Kṛta, Tretā, and the other [yugas], the footrest for the seat of Śiva;

74.s:
dharmaṃ jñānañca vairāgyamaiśvaryañcāgnidiṅmukhān /
kūrpārakuṅkumasvarṇakajjalābhān yajet kramāt //
74.d:
धर्मं ज्ञानञ्च वैराग्यमैश्वर्यञ्चाग्निदिङ्मुखान् /
कूर्पारकुङ्कुमस्वर्णकज्जलाभान् यजेत् क्रमात् //
74.m: Dharma, Knowledge, Dispassion, and Sovereignty, facing the directions beginning with fire [southeast], / having the luster of camphor, saffron, gold, and collyrium, one should worship in sequence;

74.s:
padmañca karṇikāmadhye pūrvādau madhyato nava /
varadābhayahastāś ca śaktayo dhṛtacāmarāḥ //
74.d:
पद्मञ्च कर्णिकामध्ये पूर्वादौ मध्यतो नव /
वरदाभयहस्ताश् च शक्तयो धृतचामराः //
74.m: and the lotus in the middle of the pericarp, the nine [śaktis] from the east and in the centre, / having hands granting boons and fearlessness, and holding chowries:

74.s:
vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca kālī kalavikāriṇī /
balavikaraṇī pūjyā balapramathanī kramāt //
74.d:
वामा ज्येष्ठा च रौद्री च काली कलविकारिणी /
बलविकरणी पूज्या बलप्रमथनी क्रमात् //
74.m: Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikāriṇī, / Balavikaraṇī, and Balapramathanī are to be worshipped in sequence;

74.s:
hāṃ sarvabhūtadamanī keśarāgre manonmanī /
kṣittyādi śuddhavidyāntu tattvavyāpakamāsanaṃ //
74.d:
हां सर्वभूतदमनी केशराग्रे मनोन्मनी /
क्षित्त्यादि शुद्धविद्यान्तु तत्त्वव्यापकमासनं //
74.m: 'hāṃ' Sarvabhūtadamanī, and Manonmanī at the tip of the filaments; / the seat pervades the principles beginning with earth and ending with Śuddhavidyā.

74.s:
nyaset siṃhāsane devaṃ śuklaṃ pañcamukhaṃ vibhuṃ /
daśabāhuṃ ca khaṇḍenduṃ dadhānandakṣiṇaiḥ karaiḥ //
74.d:
न्यसेत् सिंहासने देवं शुक्लं पञ्चमुखं विभुं /
दशबाहुं च खण्डेन्दुं दधानन्दक्षिणैः करैः //
74.m: One should deposit on the lion-throne the god: white, five-faced, the all-pervading lord, / ten-armed, holding the crescent moon with his right hands,

74.s:
śaktyṛṣṭiśūlakhaṭvāṅgavaradaṃ vāmakaiḥ karaiḥ /
ḍamaruṃ vījapurañca nīlābjaṃ sūtrakotpalaṃ //
74.d:
शक्त्यृष्टिशूलखट्वाङ्गवरदं वामकैः करैः /
डमरुं वीजपुरञ्च नीलाब्जं सूत्रकोत्पलं //
74.m: granting boons with a spear, dart, trident, and staff (khaṭvāṅga); with his left hands, / [holding] a drum, a citron, a blue lotus, a thread, and a water lily;

74.s:
dvātriṃśallakṣaṇopetāṃ śaivīṃ mūrtintu madhyataḥ /
hāṃ haṃ hāṃ śivamūrtaye svaprakāśaṃ śivaṃ smaran //
74.d:
द्वात्रिंशल्लक्षणोपेतां शैवीं मूर्तिन्तु मध्यतः /
हां हं हां शिवमूर्तये स्वप्रकाशं शिवं स्मरन् //
74.m: the Śaiva icon endowed with thirty-two marks in the centre; / [saying] 'hāṃ haṃ hāṃ to the Śiva-icon', remembering Śiva who is self-luminous.

74.s:
brahmādikāraṇatyāgānmantraṃ nītvā śivāspadaṃ /
tato lalātamadhyasthaṃ sphurattārāpatiprabhaṃ //
74.d:
ब्रह्मादिकारणत्यागान्मन्त्रं नीत्वा शिवास्पदं /
ततो ललातमध्यस्थं स्फुरत्तारापतिप्रभं //
74.m: Having led the mantra to Śiva's abode by relinquishing Brahmā and the other causal deities, / then [Śiva] situated in the middle of the forehead, possessing the brilliance of the flashing moon,

74.s:
ṣaḍaṅgena samākīrṇaṃ vindurūpaṃ paraṃ śivaṃ /
puṣpāñjaligataṃ dhyātvā lakṣmīmūrtau niveśayet //
74.d:
षडङ्गेन समाकीर्णं विन्दुरूपं परं शिवं /
पुष्पाञ्जलिगतं ध्यात्वा लक्ष्मीमूर्तौ निवेशयेत् //
74.m: accompanied by the six limbs, Supreme Śiva in the form of a bindu; / having meditated upon him in a folded-hand offering of flowers, one should install him in the auspicious icon.

74.s:
oṃ hāṃ hauṃ śivāya nama āvāhanyā hṛddā tataḥ /
āvāhya sthāpya sthāpanyā sannidhāyāntikaṃ śivaṃ //
74.d:
ओं हां हौं शिवाय नम आवाहन्या हृद्दा ततः /
आवाह्य स्थाप्य स्थापन्या सन्निधायान्तिकं शिवं //
74.m: [Saying] 'oṃ hāṃ hauṃ obeisance to Śiva', with the invoking gesture (āvāhanī) and the Hṛdaya mantra then, / having invoked him, installed him with the installing gesture (sthāpanī), bringing Śiva into proximity,

74.s:
nirodhayenniṣṭhurayā kālakāntyā phaḍantataḥ /
:p 216
vighnānutsārya viṣṭhyātha(1) liṅgamudrāṃ namaskṛtiṃ //
74.d:
निरोधयेन्निष्ठुरया कालकान्त्या फडन्ततः /
:प् 216
विघ्नानुत्सार्य विष्ठ्याथ(1) लिङ्गमुद्रां नमस्कृतिं //
74.m:
one should restrain him with the Niṣṭhurā gesture, [with the mantra] Kālakānti ending in 'phaṭ'.
[Page 216]
Having dispelled obstacles with the Viṣṭhi gesture, then [presenting] the liṅga gesture and obeisance,

74.s:
hṛdāvaguṇṭhayet paścādāvāhaḥ sammukhī tataḥ /
niveśanaṃ sthāpanaṃ syātsannidhānaṃ tavāsmi bhoḥ //
74.d:
हृदावगुण्ठयेत् पश्चादावाहः सम्मुखी ततः /
निवेशनं स्थापनं स्यात्सन्निधानं तवास्मि भोः //
74.m: one should veil him with the Hṛdaya mantra afterwards. Then invocation means turning towards; / installation is placement; proximity means 'O Lord, I am yours'.

74.s:
ākarmakāṇḍaparyantaṃ sannedheyoparikṣayaḥ /
svabhakteś ca(2) prakāśoyastadbhavedavaguṇṭhanaṃ //
74.d:
आकर्मकाण्डपर्यन्तं सन्नेधेयोपरिक्षयः /
स्वभक्तेश् च(2) प्रकाशोयस्तद्भवेदवगुण्ठनं //
74.m: The end of the upward destruction of proximity lasts until the ritual section; / and the illumination of one's own devotion: that is veiling.

74.s:
sakalīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā mantraiḥ ṣaḍbhirathaikatāṃ /
aṅgānāmaṅginā sārdhaṃ vidadhyādamṛtīkṛtaṃ //
74.d:
सकलीकरणं कृत्वा मन्त्रैः षड्भिरथैकतां /
अङ्गानामङ्गिना सार्धं विदध्यादमृतीकृतं //
74.m: Having performed the bodily integration (sakalīkaraṇa) with the six mantras, one should then effect the oneness / of the limbs with the possessor of the limbs, rendered immortal.

74.s:
cicchaktihṛdayaṃ śambhoḥ śiva aiśvaryamaṣṭadhā(3) /
śikhāvaśitvaṃ cābhedyaṃ tejaḥ kavacamaiśvaraṃ //
74.d:
चिच्छक्तिहृदयं शम्भोः शिव ऐश्वर्यमष्टधा(3) /
शिखावशित्वं चाभेद्यं तेजः कवचमैश्वरं //
74.m: The heart of Śambhu is the consciousness-power; the head is the eightfold sovereignty; / the tuft is mastery; and the divine armor is impenetrable splendor.

74.s:
pratāpo duḥsahaścāstramantarāyāpahārakaṃ /
namaḥ svadhā ca svāhā ca vauṣaṭ ceti yathākramaṃ //
74.d:
प्रतापो दुःसहश्चास्त्रमन्तरायापहारकं /
नमः स्वधा च स्वाहा च वौषट् चेति यथाक्रमं //
74.m: The weapon is irresistible majesty, which removes obstacles. / [The mantras end with] "namaḥ", "svadhā", "svāhā", and "vauṣaṭ", in due order.

74.s:
hṛtpuraḥsaramuccārya pādyādīni nivedayet /
pādyaṃ pādāmbujadvandve vaktreṣvācamanīyakaṃ //
74.d:
हृत्पुरःसरमुच्चार्य पाद्यादीनि निवेदयेत् /
पाद्यं पादाम्बुजद्वन्द्वे वक्त्रेष्वाचमनीयकं //
74.m: Pronouncing them preceded by the heart [mantra], one should offer water for washing the feet and so forth: / water for the feet at the pair of lotus feet; sipping-water at the mouths;

74.s:
arghyaṃ śirasi devasya dūrvāpuṣpākṣatāni ca /
evaṃ saṃskṛtya saṃskārair daśabhiḥ parameśvaraṃ //
74.d:
अर्घ्यं शिरसि देवस्य दूर्वापुष्पाक्षतानि च /
एवं संस्कृत्य संस्कारैर् दशभिः परमेश्वरं //
74.m: water offering at the head of the god, along with dūrvā grass, flowers, and unbroken grains. / Having thus consecrated the Supreme Lord with the ten consecrations,

74.s:
yajet pañcopacāreṇa vidhinā kusumādibhiḥ /
abhyukṣyoddhartya nirmbhañjya rājikālavaṇādibhiḥ //
74.d:
यजेत् पञ्चोपचारेण विधिना कुसुमादिभिः /
अभ्युक्ष्योद्धर्त्य निर्म्भञ्ज्य राजिकालवणादिभिः //
74.m: one should worship him with the fivefold offerings of flowers and so forth according to rule. / Having sprinkled, rubbed, and warded off [evil] with mustard seeds, salt, and so forth,

74.s:
arghyodavindupuṣpādyair gaḍḍūkaiḥ(4) snāpayecchanaiḥ /
payodadhighṛtakṣaudraśarkarādyair anukramāt //
74.d:
अर्घ्योदविन्दुपुष्पाद्यैर् गड्डूकैः(4) स्नापयेच्छनैः /
पयोदधिघृतक्षौद्रशर्कराद्यैर् अनुक्रमात् //
74.m: one should slowly bathe him with water offerings, drops of water, flowers, and so forth, from water-pots, / and successively with milk, curds, clarified butter, honey, and sugar,

74.s:
īśādimantritardravyair arcya teṣāṃ(5) viparyayaḥ /
:n
1 choṭyātha iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 abhuktejyā iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 śivamaiśvaryamaṣṭadhā iti ga, gha,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
4 gandhakair iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 ity ādimantritair bhakṣyaiś caiṣāmiti kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 217
toyadhūpāntaraiḥ sarvair mūlena snapayecchivaṃ //
74.d:
ईशादिमन्त्रितर्द्रव्यैर् अर्च्य तेषां(5) विपर्ययः /
:न्
1 छोट्याथ इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 अभुक्तेज्या इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 शिवमैश्वर्यमष्टधा इति ग, घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
4 गन्धकैर् इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 इत्य् आदिमन्त्रितैर् भक्ष्यैश् चैषामिति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 217
तोयधूपान्तरैः सर्वैर् मूलेन स्नपयेच्छिवं //
74.m:
consecrated with the mantras beginning with Īśāna and worshiped with the substances, or in reverse order.
[Gap in text]
1. "choṭyātha" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "abhuktejyā" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ga.
3. "śivamaiśvaryamaṣṭadhā" is the variant reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and gha.
4. "gandhakaiḥ" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked kha.
5. "ity ādimantritair bhakṣyaiś caiṣām" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked kha. / Page 217
One should bathe Śiva with the root mantra, interspersing all [substances] with water and incense.

74.s:
virūkṣya yavacūrṇena yatheṣṭaṃ śītalair jalaiḥ /
svaśaktyā gandhatoyena saṃsnāpya śucivāsasā //
74.d:
विरूक्ष्य यवचूर्णेन यथेष्टं शीतलैर् जलैः /
स्वशक्त्या गन्धतोयेन संस्नाप्य शुचिवाससा //
74.m: Having rubbed [him] with barley powder and, at will, with cool waters, / and having bathed him according to one's capacity with scented water, [one should dry him] with a clean cloth.

74.s:
nirmārjyārghyaṃ pradadyācca nopari bhrāmayet karaṃ /
na śūnyamastakaṃ liṅgaṃ puṣpaiḥ kuryāttato dadet //
74.d:
निर्मार्ज्यार्घ्यं प्रदद्याच्च नोपरि भ्रामयेत् करं /
न शून्यमस्तकं लिङ्गं पुष्पैः कुर्यात्ततो ददेत् //
74.m: Having wiped [him], one should offer a water offering; one must not circle the hand over the top; / one should not leave the head of the liṅga bare of flowers; then one should present them.

74.s:
candanādyaiḥ samālabhya puṣpaiḥ prārcya śivāṇunā(1) /
dhūpabhājanamastreṇa prokṣyābhyarcya śivāṇunā(2) //
74.d:
चन्दनाद्यैः समालभ्य पुष्पैः प्रार्च्य शिवाणुना(1) /
धूपभाजनमस्त्रेण प्रोक्ष्याभ्यर्च्य शिवाणुना(2) //
74.m: Having anointed [him] with sandalwood paste and so forth, and having worshiped him with flowers using the Śiva-mantra, / having sprinkled the incense burner with the weapon [mantra] and worshiped it with the Śiva-mantra,

74.s:
astreṇa pūjitāṃ ghaṇṭāṃ cādāya guggulaṃ dadet /
dadyādācamanaṃ paścāt svadhāntaṃ hṛdayāṇunā(3) //
74.d:
अस्त्रेण पूजितां घण्टां चादाय गुग्गुलं ददेत् /
दद्यादाचमनं पश्चात् स्वधान्तं हृदयाणुना(3) //
74.m: and having taken up the bell worshiped with the weapon [mantra], one should offer bdellium resin. / Afterward, one should offer sipping-water ending with "svadhā" using the heart mantra.

74.s:
ārātrikaṃ samuttārya tathaivācāmayet punaḥ /
praṇamyādāya devājñāṃ bhogāṅgāni prapūjayet //
74.d:
आरात्रिकं समुत्तार्य तथैवाचामयेत् पुनः /
प्रणम्यादाय देवाज्ञां भोगाङ्गानि प्रपूजयेत् //
74.m: Having waved the waving-lamp (ārātrika) and likewise offered sipping-water again, / having bowed and received the command of the god, one should worship the enjoyable limbs:

74.s:
hṛdagnau candrabhaṃ caiśe śivaṃ cāmīkaraprabhaṃ /
śikhāṃ raktāñca nairṛtye kṛṣṇaṃ varma ca vāyave //
74.d:
हृदग्नौ चन्द्रभं चैशे शिवं चामीकरप्रभं /
शिखां रक्ताञ्च नैरृत्ये कृष्णं वर्म च वायवे //
74.m: in the southeast, the heart resembling the moon; in the northeast, Śiva shining like gold; / in the southwest, the red tuft; and in the northwest, the black armor.

74.s:
caturvaktraṃ caturbāhuṃ(4) dalasthān(5) pūjayedimān /
daṃṣṭrākarālamapyastraṃ pūrvādau vajrasannibhaṃ //
74.d:
चतुर्वक्त्रं चतुर्बाहुं(4) दलस्थान्(5) पूजयेदिमान् /
दंष्ट्राकरालमप्यस्त्रं पूर्वादौ वज्रसन्निभं //
74.m: One should worship these situated on the petals, having four faces and four arms; / and the weapon, fierce with fangs, resembling the thunderbolt, in the east and other [directions]:

74.s:
mūle hauṃ śivāya namaḥ oṃ hāṃ hūṃ hīṃ hoṃ śiraś ca /
hṛṃ śikhāyai haiṃ varma haścāstraṃ parivārayutāya ca //
74.d:
मूले हौं शिवाय नमः ओं हां हूं हीं हों शिरश् च /
हृं शिखायै हैं वर्म हश्चास्त्रं परिवारयुताय च //
74.m: "At the root: hauṃ śivāya namaḥ; oṃ hāṃ hūṃ hīṃ hoṃ, and the head; / hṛṃ to the tuft; haiṃ to the armor; and haḥ to the weapon, and to him accompanied by his retinue."

74.s:
śivāya dadyāt pādyañca ācāmañcārghyameva ca /
gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpadīpaṃ naivedyācamanīyakaṃ //
74.d:
शिवाय दद्यात् पाद्यञ्च आचामञ्चार्घ्यमेव च /
गन्धं पुष्पं धूपदीपं नैवेद्याचमनीयकं //
74.m: To Śiva one should offer water for the feet, sipping-water, and the water offering, / perfume, flowers, incense, a lamp, food offering, and sipping-water,

74.s:
karodvartanatāmbūlaṃ mukhavāsañca darpaṇaṃ /
:n
1 śivātmaneti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 śivātmaneti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 hṛdayātmaneti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 caturvaktrāṃś caturbāhūn iti gha, ṅa,
cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
5 dalāgre iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 218
śirasyāropya devasya dūrvākṣatapavitrakaṃ //
74.d:
करोद्वर्तनताम्बूलं मुखवासञ्च दर्पणं /
:न्
1 शिवात्मनेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 शिवात्मनेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 हृदयात्मनेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 चतुर्वक्त्रांश् चतुर्बाहून् इति घ, ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
5 दलाग्रे इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 218
शिरस्यारोप्य देवस्य दूर्वाक्षतपवित्रकं //
74.m:
unguent for the hands, betel, mouth-perfume, and a mirror.
[Gap in text]
1. "śivātmanā" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "śivātmanā" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked kha.
3. "hṛdayātmanā" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked kha.
3. "caturvaktrāṃś caturbāhūn" is the variant reading in the two manuscripts marked gha and ṅa.
5. "dalāgre" is the variant reading in the manuscript marked ṅa. / Page 218
Having placed upon the head of the god a pavitraka along with dūrvā grass and unbroken grains,

74.s:
mūlamaṣṭaśataṃ japtvā hṛdayenābhimantritaṃ /
carmaṇāveṣṭitaṃ khaḍgaṃ rakṣitaṃ kuśapuṣpakaiḥ //
74.d:
मूलमष्टशतं जप्त्वा हृदयेनाभिमन्त्रितं /
चर्मणावेष्टितं खड्गं रक्षितं कुशपुष्पकैः //
74.m: having recited the root mantra one hundred and eight times, consecrated it with the heart [mantra], / [and having visualized] a sword enveloped in skin, protected with kuśa grass and flowers,

74.s:
akṣatair mudrāyā yuktaṃ śivamudbhavasañjñayā /
guhyātiguhyaguptyarthaṃ(1) gṛhāṇāsmatkṛtaṃ japaṃ //
74.d:
अक्षतैर् मुद्राया युक्तं शिवमुद्भवसञ्ज्ञया /
गुह्यातिगुह्यगुप्त्यर्थं(1) गृहाणास्मत्कृतं जपं //
74.m: accompanied by unbroken grains and the mudrā known as Udbhava: / "For the sake of guarding the secret of secrets, accept the recitation performed by us,

74.s:
siddhirbhavatu me yena(2) tvatprasādāttvayi sthite /
bhogī ślokaṃ paṭhitvādyaṃ(3) dakṣahastena śambhave //
74.d:
सिद्धिर्भवतु मे येन(2) त्वत्प्रसादात्त्वयि स्थिते /
भोगी श्लोकं पठित्वाद्यं(3) दक्षहस्तेन शम्भवे //
74.m: by which may accomplishment be mine, by your grace, while abiding in you." / The enjoyer, having recited this first verse, [presents it] to Śambhu with the right hand;

74.s:
mūlāṇunārghyatoyena varahaste(4) nivedayet /
yatkiñcit kurmahe deva sadā sukṛtaduskṛtaṃ //
74.d:
मूलाणुनार्घ्यतोयेन वरहस्ते(4) निवेदयेत् /
यत्किञ्चित् कुर्महे देव सदा सुकृतदुस्कृतं //
74.m: with the root mantra, he should offer it into [his] boon-granting hand with arghya water: / "Whatever good deed or bad deed we do always, O Lord,

74.s:
tanme śivapadasthasya hūṃ kṣaḥ kṣepaya śaṅkara /
śivo dātā śivo bhoktā śivaḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat //
74.d:
तन्मे शिवपदस्थस्य हूं क्षः क्षेपय शङ्कर /
शिवो दाता शिवो भोक्ता शिवः सर्वमिदं जगत् //
74.m: dispel that for me, who abide in the state of Śiva, hūṃ kṣaḥ, O Śaṅkara! / Śiva is the giver, Śiva is the enjoyer, Śiva is this entire world;

74.s:
śivo jayati sarvatra yaḥ śivaḥ sohameva ca /
ślokadvayamadhītyaivaṃ japaṃ devāya cārpayet //
74.d:
शिवो जयति सर्वत्र यः शिवः सोहमेव च /
श्लोकद्वयमधीत्यैवं जपं देवाय चार्पयेत् //
74.m: Śiva is victorious everywhere; that which is Śiva, that indeed am I." / Having thus recited these two verses, one should surrender the recitation to the god.

74.s:
śivāṅgānāṃ(5) daśāṃśañca datvārghyaṃ stutimācaret /
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya nameccāṣṭāṅgañcāṣṭamūrtaye(6) /
natvā dhyānādibhiś caiva yajeccitre 'nalādiṣu //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye śivapūjā nāma catuḥsaptatitamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 guhyātiguhyagoptā tvamiti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 siddhirbhavatu me deveti kha, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 paṭhitvāmumiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 harahaste iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 śivajñānāmiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 namedaṣtāṅgamūrtaye iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 219
:ś atha pañcasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
agnisthāpanādividhiḥ
74.d:
शिवाङ्गानां(5) दशांशञ्च दत्वार्घ्यं स्तुतिमाचरेत् /
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य नमेच्चाष्टाङ्गञ्चाष्टमूर्तये(6) /
नत्वा ध्यानादिभिश् चैव यजेच्चित्रे ऽनलादिषु //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये शिवपूजा नाम चतुःसप्ततितमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 गुह्यातिगुह्यगोप्ता त्वमिति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 सिद्धिर्भवतु मे देवेति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 पठित्वामुमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 हरहस्ते इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 शिवज्ञानामिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 नमेदष्ताङ्गमूर्तये इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 219
:श् अथ पञ्चसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
अग्निस्थापनादिविधिः
74.m:
Having offered an arghya worth a tenth part to the limbs of Śiva, one should perform praise. / Having circumambulated, one should bow with the eight limbs to the eightfold form; / and having bowed, one should worship [him] through meditation and other rites in paintings, fire, and so forth.
Thus ends the seventy-fourth chapter, named "The Worship of Śiva", in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
